Core Workflow

1. Install and scaffold

genai-tk is not on PyPI. Install from git with uv, then scaffold:

uv init my-app && cd my-app
uv add "genai-tk @ git+https://github.com/tclatos/genai-tk@main"
uv run cli init --name "My Agent App"                  # scaffolds config/, skills/, justfile; runs uv sync
uv run cli init --extra harnessing --extra browser     # also install DeepAgents/DeerFlow + Playwright
just run                                               # uv run cli agent chat

Extras: harnessing (deepagents, DeerFlow, OpenSandbox), browser, nlp, postgres, streamlit, baml, chromadb, docling, monitoring, and all (everything except monitoring). Put API keys in .env (auto-loaded, plus ~/.env for the CLI). Run uv run cli info doctor as a pre-flight check.

2. Call models

from genai_tk.core.factories import get_llm, get_embeddings

llm = get_llm()                                  # llm.models.default from the active profile
llm = get_llm("fast_model")                      # a tag under llm.models
llm = get_llm("gpt-4o-mini@openai")              # model_id@provider (resolved via models.dev)
llm = get_llm("parrot_local@fake")               # offline fake model, no API key
llm = get_llm("o3 (high)@openai")                # inline reasoning effort
llm = get_llm("claude-haiku@openrouter:speed")   # gateway routing strategy
llm = get_llm("gpt-4o-mini@openai", streaming=True, json_mode=True, cache="sqlite")

embeddings = get_embeddings()                    # embeddings.models.default

Both return plain LangChain BaseChatModel / Embeddings objects. CLI: cli core llm -i "hello" -m parrot_local@fake, cli info models, cli info llm-profile <id>. Details in models.md.

3. Define an agent in YAML, run it anywhere

Profiles live under a top-level agents: dict keyed by slug, in config/agents.yaml or config/agents/*.yaml. agent_defaults: supplies fallbacks for LangChain profiles.

# config/agents.yaml
agent_defaults:
  type: react
  default_profile: research
agents:
  research:
    harness: langchain            # langchain (default) | deerflow
    name: "Research"
    type: deep                    # react | deep | custom
    llm: gpt-4o-mini@openai
    system_prompt: "You are an expert researcher. Cite sources."
    tools:
      - genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_function:
          verbose: false
    mcp_servers: [filesystem]     # names from mcpServers: in mcp_servers.yaml
    skill_directories: ["${paths.project}/skills"]
    enable_planning: true
    enable_file_system: true
    checkpointer: {type: memory}  # none | memory | class
from genai_tk.agents.langchain import LangchainAgent

agent = LangchainAgent("research", llm="claude-haiku@openrouter")   # slug or display name, + overrides
print(agent.run("Summarise this week's AI news"))
uv run cli agents list
uv run cli agents run research "Summarise this week's AI news"
uv run cli agents run research --chat

For a harness-agnostic API (LangChain and DeerFlow behind one event stream), use genai_tk.agents.harness.create_harness("research"). See agents.md.

4. Add RAG, workflows, or structured extraction

embeddings_store:
  chroma:
    backend: genai_tk.core.vector_backends.ChromaBackend
    embeddings: default
    config: {storage: "${paths.data_root}/vector_store"}
retrievers:
  docs: {type: genai_tk.core.retrievers.VectorRetriever, embeddings_store: chroma, top_k: 4}
uv run cli rag add-files ./docs -r docs -p "**/*.md"
uv run cli rag query "What does the doc say about X?" -r docs
uv run cli workflow run markdownize/fast --set sources=./inbox --set md_output_dir=./data/md
uv run cli baml run ExtractResume -i "John Smith; 10 years Python"         # a function from your baml_src/

Configuration in One Minute

config/app_conf.yaml is the root. It is loaded from config/app_conf.yaml relative to the current working directory (it does not walk up parent directories), so run commands from the project root.

profile: ${oc.env:GENAITK_PROFILE,local}
paths:
  project: ${oc.env:PWD}
  config: ${paths.project}/config
  data_root: ${paths.project}/data
:merge: ["**/*.yaml", "!demos/**", "!examples/agents/**"]   # gitignore-style globs under config/
:profiles:
  local:
    llm: {models: {default: gpt-4o-mini@openai, fake: parrot_local@fake}, cache: sqlite}
    embeddings: {models: {default: embeddings_768@fake}}
:env: {LOGURU_LEVEL: INFO}
from genai_tk.config_mgmt.config_mngr import global_config, switch_profile

cfg = global_config()
cfg.get_str("llm.models.default")
cfg.section("my_feature", MyFeatureConfig)      # typed Pydantic access; empty model if absent
switch_profile("pytest")                         # sets GENAITK_PROFILE and reloads

Full semantics in configuration.md.

Coding Conventions (from upstream AGENTS.md)

  • Python 3.12+: str | None, list[str]; avoid Any (use discriminated unions or TypeAlias)
  • Absolute imports only; ruff with line length 120
  • Pydantic v2 for all structured data: model_config = {...}, model_post_init(), model_dump_json(); no dataclasses, unnamed tuples, or untyped dicts
  • loguru for logging; Google-style docstrings without types or Raises:
  • Read config through typed models: global_config().section(...) / .section_dict(...)
  • Tests: use the fake_llm_id / fake_llm fixtures and fake providers instead of mocks; never hard-code model IDs
  • Domain knowledge goes in SKILL.md files loaded on demand, not in system prompts

Upstream Doc Drift

These upstream docs or bundled skills contradict the code at 7fbd7a3. Use the right-hand column.

Docs sayCode does
Config search walks up parent directoriesOnly config/app_conf.yaml under the CWD
`cli init -t agent-app\rag-app\workflow-app\minimal, --with-deer-flow`Flags are --name, --extra, --with-graph, --graph-path, --force
`cli mcp serve\list\generate`The group is `cli mcpserver start\serve\list\generate`
cli core decisioncli core classifier
get_llm(..., reasoning={...})Raises; use "model (high)@provider" or reasoning_effort="high"
Workflow DSL with steps: / uses: / needs:run: or pipeline: with id, run, after, with
cli rag add-files <retriever> <dir>, --includecli rag add-files <dir> -r <retriever> -p <pathspec>
Short retriever/backend aliases (type: vector, backend: Chroma)Fully qualified class paths are required
langchain_agents: profile listsagents: dict + agent_defaults:
baml_invoke(inputs=...), cli baml extract --recursive --includebaml_invoke(name, params, ...), -p <pathspec> (default **/*.md)
Bundled baml_extract, rag_ingest, office2pdf workflows (and cli baml extract) just workTheir YAML param names don't match the flow signatures; see workflows.md

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

  • Using pre-2026 import paths — genai_tk.core.llm_factory, genai_tk.utils.config_mngr, and genai_tk.core.retriever_factory are gone with no shims; import from genai_tk.core.factories and genai_tk.config_mgmt.config_mngr
  • Writing langchain_agents: / profiles: lists or spec: web_search tools — the old profile schema is rejected; use the agents: dict and qualified factory paths for tools
  • Putting skills: on a profile — it is silently ignored; use skill_directories: (deep agents only)
  • Bare model names in YAML — gpt-4o-mini triggers fuzzy lookup; always write model_id@provider
  • Short aliases for retrievers and vector backends — they fail to resolve; use genai_tk.core.retrievers.VectorRetriever, genai_tk.core.vector_backends.ChromaBackend, etc.
  • Hard-coding agents or LLMs in Python — add a YAML entry; LangchainAgent("slug") only loads and overrides
  • type: deep or DeerFlow without the harnessing extra — deepagents and deerflow-harness live there
  • Expecting --sandbox on cli agents run to isolate a LangChain profile — it only applies to DeerFlow; set backend: {type: docker} (or LangchainAgent(..., sandbox="docker")) for LangChain profiles
  • Running from a subdirectory — config discovery is CWD-relative; ConfigFileNotFoundError usually means you are not at the project root
  • Copying examples from upstream docs/ without checking the code — see "Upstream Doc Drift"

When to Use / Not Use

Use this skill when:

  • Working inside a genai-tk project (a config/app_conf.yaml and genai_tk imports are present)
  • Writing or fixing agent profiles, provider/LLM config, retrievers, workflows, or cli.commands entries
  • Scaffolding with cli init, extending the CLI, or wiring MCP servers, sandboxes, BAML, or trajectories
  • Migrating code written for older genai-tk versions (old imports, langchain_agents:, SmolAgents)

Do NOT use this skill when:

  • The project uses plain LangChain/LangGraph without genai-tk — use the langchain skill
  • You need a quick standalone agent without config-first machinery — the smolagents or langchain skills fit better
  • The question is about DeerFlow or DeepAgents used directly, outside genai-tk's harness

documents.label: Agents — references/agents.md
documents.html:
Agents — references/agents.md

genai-tk runs agents through two harnesses that share YAML profiles, the LLM factory, MCP servers, sandboxes, and skills:

HarnessProfile typeEngineNeeds
langchain (default)reactlangchain.agents.create_agentcore
langchaindeepdeepagents.create_deep_agent (planning, file system, subagents, skills)harnessing extra
langchaincustomgenai_tk.extra.langgraphs.custom_react_agent.create_custom_react_agentcore
deerflow— (`mode: flash\thinking\pro\ultra`)ByteDance DeerFlow, embedded in-processharnessing extra

SmolAgents is no longer an agent framework in genai-tk (cli agents smolagents, SmolAgent, and config/smolagents.yaml are gone). Its code-first style lives on as CodeAct, a deep profile whose only tool is a Python executor (see below).

Profiles

Where they live

Profiles are loaded from the first of these that exists:

  1. config/agents.yaml
  2. config/agents/*.yaml (not recursive)
  3. config/examples/agents/ (bundled examples)
  4. config/examples/agents.yaml

Because the lookup stops at the first match, creating config/agents.yaml hides the bundled examples. Copy any example profiles you still want.

Schema

agent_defaults:                    # fallbacks for harness: langchain profiles only
  type: react
  llm: null                        # null → llm.models.default
  middlewares:
    - class: genai_tk.agents.langchain.middleware.rich_middleware.RichToolCallMiddleware
  checkpointer: {type: none}
  backend: {type: none}
  enable_planning: true
  enable_file_system: true
  skills:
    directories: ["${paths.project}/skills"]
  default_profile: research        # used by `cli agents run` without a profile

agents:                            # dict keyed by slug; the slug is the CLI/Python key
  research:
    harness: langchain
    name: "Research"               # display name (defaults to the slug)
    type: deep
    description: "Web researcher that writes cited reports"
    llm: gpt-4o-mini@openai
    system_prompt: |
      You are an expert researcher. Plan with write_todos, cite every source.
    tools:
      - genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_function:
          verbose: false
    mcp_servers: [filesystem]
    skill_directories: ["${paths.project}/skills/runtime", "${paths.project}/skills/custom"]
    middlewares:
      - class: genai_tk.agents.langchain.middleware.rich_middleware.RichToolCallMiddleware
      - class: genai_tk.agents.langchain.middleware.observation_truncation_middleware.ObservationTruncationMiddleware
        max_chars: 12000
    backend: {type: aio_sandbox, startup_timeout: 90.0}
    checkpointer: {type: memory}
    recursion_limit: 100
    examples:
      - "Compare the latest open-weight coding models"

LangChain profile fields (AgentProfileConfig):

FieldNotes
harnesslangchain (default) or deerflow
name, descriptionDisplay metadata; lookups match slug or name, case-insensitively
typereact (default) \deep \custom
llmmodel_id@provider or a tag; null uses the global default
system_prompt, pre_promptKeep prompts here, not in Python
toolsQualified factory/class/function paths (see "Tools")
mcp_serversNames from mcpServers: in mcp_servers.yaml
middlewares- class: dotted.Path with constructor kwargs as sibling keys
skill_directoriesDirectories of SKILL.md files (deep agents only)
enable_planning, enable_file_systemDeep-agent built-ins (both default true)
backendnone \filesystem (root_dir) \aio_sandbox / docker \local \class (class, kwargs)
checkpointernone \memory \class (e.g. class: langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite:SqliteSaver)
subagentsDeep-agent subagents, each with name, description, system_prompt, tools
excluded_toolsDrop built-in tools by name
fs_permissionsDeep-agent filesystem rules: `operations: [read\write], paths: [...], mode: deny\allow\interrupt`
recursion_limitDefault 100
features, examplesShown in cli agents list and the webapp

Gotchas:

  • Unknown keys are silently ignored. A typo such as skills: on a profile (instead of skill_directories:) does nothing. Only agent_defaults.skills.directories is read.
  • Defaults are replaced, not merged. A profile's own middlewares: list replaces the default list entirely.
  • The old langchain_agents: {defaults, default_profile, profiles: [...]} schema and deerflow_agents: lists are no longer supported; one bundled file (config/agents/langchain/browser.yaml) still uses it and is never loaded.

Running Agents

CLI

uv run cli agents list                                   # all profiles across both harnesses
uv run cli agents run research "Summarise this week's AI news"
uv run cli agents run research --chat                    # REPL (forces a memory checkpointer)
uv run cli agents run research --chat --thread-id t42    # resume a thread
uv run cli agents run research -m claude-haiku@openrouter "..."   # LLM override
uv run cli agents run research --mcp playwright "..."    # extra MCP server (repeatable)
uv run cli agents run research "..." --json              # NDJSON harness events
echo "question" | uv run cli agents run research
uv run cli agents tui "Research Assistant"               # DeerFlow TUI (--resume, --continue)

--mode and --sandbox/-b only apply to DeerFlow profiles. For LangChain profiles, set backend: in YAML or use LangchainAgent(..., sandbox="docker").

LangchainAgent

from genai_tk.agents.langchain import LangchainAgent

agent = LangchainAgent("research")                       # slug or display name
print(agent.run("What is RAG?"))                         # sync

result = await agent.arun("Explain it like I'm 5")
async for chunk in agent.astream("Tell me a story"):     # yields str
    print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
await agent.arun_shell()                                 # interactive REPL

async with LangchainAgent("research", checkpointer=True) as agent:
    await agent.arun("Remember: my project is called Atlas")
    await agent.arun("What is my project called?")       # same thread ("1")

Constructor fields (one of profile_name or llm is required):

FieldTypeNotes
profile_name`str \None`First positional argument
llm`str \None`Override the profile's LLM, or anchor an ad-hoc agent with no profile
toolslist[BaseTool]Appended to the profile's tools
agent_type`"react" \"deep" \"custom" \None`Override the profile type
system_prompt`str \None`Override
mcp_serverslist[str]Extra MCP servers
extra_middlewareslist[str]Short names: AnonymizationMiddleware, RichToolCallMiddleware, EmptyResponseRetryMiddleware, DeduplicateToolCallsMiddleware, ObservationTruncationMiddleware, WrapUpMiddleware
checkpointerboolIn-memory checkpointing; the thread id is fixed at "1"
detailsboolVerbose tool-call panels
sandbox`"local" \"docker" \None`docker sets a Docker backend and promotes the profile to deep
vnc, keep_sandboxboolDocker sandbox VNC viewer; keep the container between runs
from langchain_core.tools import tool


@tool
def get_stock(sku: str) -> int:
    """Return the stock level for a SKU."""
    return INVENTORY.get(sku, 0)


agent = LangchainAgent(llm="gpt-4o-mini@openai", tools=[get_stock], system_prompt="You help warehouse staff.")

Lower level, when you need the compiled LangGraph graph or your own thread ids:

from genai_tk.agents.harness.profiles import load_langchain_profiles
from genai_tk.agents.langchain.factory import create_langchain_agent

profiles = load_langchain_profiles()
graph = await create_langchain_agent(profiles["research"], llm_override="claude-haiku@openrouter")
await graph.ainvoke(
    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Question"}]},
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "user-123"}},
)

Harness layer — one API for LangChain and DeerFlow

from genai_tk.agents.harness import create_harness, list_harness_profiles

for ref in list_harness_profiles():
    print(ref.key, ref.harness, ref.kind, ref.name)

harness = create_harness("research", llm_override="claude-haiku@openrouter")
async for event in harness.astream("Find three sources on QKD", thread_id="t1"):
    if event.kind == "token":
        print(event.text, end="")
    elif event.kind == "tool_call":
        print(f"\n→ {event.tool_name}({event.args})")
    elif event.kind == "error":
        print(f"\n✗ {event.message}")
answer = await harness.arun("Follow-up question", thread_id="t1")
await harness.aclose()
  • create_harness(key, *, llm_override=None, force_memory_checkpointer=False, mode_override=None, sandbox_override=None, extra_mcp=None, extra_tools=None); mode_override/sandbox_override are DeerFlow-only.
  • BaseHarness: astream(message, *, thread_id=None, context=None), arun(...), list_threads, list_models, list_skills, get_graph, get_checkpointer, aclose.
  • Events are frozen Pydantic models with a kind discriminator: TokenEvent (text), ThinkingEvent, NodeEvent, ToolCallEvent (tool_name, args, call_id), ToolResultEvent (tool_name, content), ArtifactEvent, ClarificationEvent, UsageEvent, ErrorEvent (message), EndEvent.
  • context= propagates user/tenant identity to tools and middlewares for access control.
  • genai_tk.agents.harness.chat_repl.run_chat_repl is the REPL used by --chat.

Tools

There are no short tool names (web_search, calculator, spec: entries are gone). Each entry is a qualified path, resolved by UnifiedToolSpec:

tools:
  - my_pkg.tools.make_tools                              # bare factory/function path
  - my_pkg.tools:MyToolClass                             # class path
  - genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_function:
      verbose: false                                     # single-key dict → kwargs
  - factory: genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.rag_tool_factory.create_rag_tool_from_config
    config: {retriever: docs, tool_name: search_docs, top_k: 5}   # target key + sibling kwargs

Target keys: tool, factory, class, function, target.

Built-in factories:

FactoryProvides
genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_function / create_search_tool / create_webpage_toolWeb search and page fetch
genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.sql_tool_factory.create_sql_tool_from_config / create_sql_toolkit_toolsSQL querying
genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.rag_tool_factory.create_rag_tool_from_configRetriever as a tool (see rag.md)
genai_tk.agents.tools.python_executor.tool.create_python_executor_toolsCodeAct python_interpreter
genai_tk.agents.tools.sandbox_browser.factory.create_sandbox_browser_toolsBrowser inside the Docker sandbox
genai_tk.agents.tools.direct_browser.factory.create_direct_browser_toolsHost Playwright browser (browser extra)

Writing your own: return a LangChain BaseTool or @tool function (or a list of them) from a create_*_tools() factory in your package, validate inputs at the boundary, and reference the factory from YAML.

Browser tools include browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill_credential, browser_read_page, browser_screenshot, browser_evaluate, and more. Always use browser_fill_credential for secrets, never browser_type.

CodeAct

CodeAct agents act by writing Python executed in an in-process AST sandbox. Sibling tools are injected as plain Python functions; print() output is the observation and final_answer(x) ends the run.

agents:
  codeact:
    harness: langchain
    name: "CodeAct"
    type: deep
    system_prompt: |
      Solve tasks only by writing Python with the python_interpreter tool.
      Tools such as web_search are Python functions. Call final_answer(result) when done.
    tools:
      - genai_tk.agents.tools.python_executor.tool.create_python_executor_tools:
          tools:
            - genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_tool
    enable_file_system: false

  codeact-orchestrator:                      # deep agent delegating code work to a subagent
    harness: langchain
    type: deep
    tools: []
    subagents:
      - name: codeact
        description: "Solves tasks by writing Python in a sandbox."
        system_prompt: "Write Python, print observations, finish with final_answer(x)."
        tools:
          - genai_tk.agents.tools.python_executor.tool.create_python_executor_tools:
              tools: [genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_tool]

The bundled versions are in config/examples/agents/codeact.yaml.

Middlewares

All live in genai_tk.agents.langchain.middleware:

MiddlewarePurpose
rich_middleware.RichToolCallMiddlewarePretty tool-call traces (details: true for full panels)
rich_middleware.ToolCallLimitMiddlewareCap tool calls (run_limit, thread_limit, exit_behavior)
empty_response_retry.EmptyResponseRetryMiddlewareRetry empty model output; always prepended automatically
deduplicate_middleware.DeduplicateToolCallsMiddlewareDrop repeated identical tool calls
observation_truncation_middleware.ObservationTruncationMiddlewareTruncate long tool outputs (max_chars)
prompt_cache.PromptCacheMiddlewareMark the static prompt prefix cacheable (Anthropic, OpenRouter passthrough)
wrap_up_middleware.WrapUpMiddlewareEscalating soft/hard limits that force convergence before the recursion limit
anonymization_middleware.AnonymizationMiddlewareReversible Presidio + Faker PII redaction (nlp extra)
sensitivity_router_middleware.SensitivityRouterMiddlewareRoute sensitive conversations to a safer LLM
skill_marks_middleware.SkillLoadMarksMiddlewareRecords skill loads in trajectories; auto-added for deep agents with skills

Third-party middlewares work the same way, for example - class: deepagents.middleware.summarization.SummarizationMiddleware.

Skills

Skills are SKILL.md files the agent reads on demand (progressive disclosure), instead of stuffing domain knowledge into the system prompt.

  • Only type: deep profiles load skills: skill_directories is passed to deepagents' native SkillsMiddleware. React agents ignore it. genai-tk itself has no SkillsMiddleware class.
  • With a Docker backend, each skill directory is bind-mounted read-only at /mnt/skills/<dirname>.
  • DeerFlow profiles use skill_directories plus an optional available_skills filter.
  • Manage skills with cli skills list|create|add|validate (see cli-and-init.md).

Sandbox

uv run cli sandbox start      # start the OpenSandbox server (generates its own config)
uv run cli sandbox pull       # pre-pull the image; cuts first-run startup from ~30s to ~5s
uv run cli sandbox status
uv run cli sandbox list
uv run cli sandbox stop

Run start + pull once per boot. The sandbox image (ghcr.io/agent-infra/sandbox) provides Python, Node.js, Chromium with VNC, and a REST file/shell API. Containers run with ulimit core=0 and isolated LibreOffice profiles. Use it for any untrusted code; local executes on the host.

backend:
  type: aio_sandbox            # or docker
  host_port: 18091
  startup_timeout: 90.0
  work_dir: /home/user
  env_vars: {MY_VAR: "1"}

MCP

Consuming MCP servers

# config/mcp_servers.yaml
mcpServers:
  filesystem:
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "${paths.project}"]
  playwright:
    command: npx
    args: ["@playwright/mcp@latest", "--headless"]
  remote_search:
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    transport: streamable-http          # stdio | sse | streamable-http | http
    headers: {Authorization: "Bearer ${oc.env:SEARCH_TOKEN}"}
    disabled: false

mcpProjectServers:                      # genai-tk servers defined in tk_servers.yaml
  chinook: {}
  search: {disabled: true}

Reference servers by name in a profile's mcp_servers: or pass --mcp NAME on the CLI. uv run cli info mcp-tools lists the tools they expose, and uv run cli core mcp-call calls one directly.

Exposing tools as an MCP server

# config/tk_servers.yaml
mcp_expose_servers:
  search:
    description: "Web search tools"
    tools:
      - factory: genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.search_tools_factory.create_search_tool
    agent:                               # optional: wrap all tools in one agent tool
      enabled: true
      name: run_search_agent
      llm: gpt-4o-mini@openai
uv run cli mcpserver list
uv run cli mcpserver start --name search --transport stdio
uv run cli mcpserver start --name search --transport streamable-http --port 8765
uv run cli mcpserver generate --name search      # emit a standalone server script

The group is mcpserver; upstream docs and comments that say cli mcp ... are out of date. The implementation targets MCP 2.0, with compatibility shims for 1.x clients in genai_tk.mcp.compat.

DeerFlow

DeerFlow profiles live under the same agents: dict with harness: deerflow. They do not inherit agent_defaults.

agents:
  "Research Assistant":
    harness: deerflow
    description: "Deep web research with reports"
    mode: pro                    # flash | thinking | pro | ultra
    llm: gpt-4o-mini@openai      # optional
    tool_groups: [web, file, bash]
    mcp_servers: [filesystem]
    skill_directories: ["${paths.project}/skills"]
    available_skills: []         # optional filter
    sandbox: docker              # local | docker
    plan_mode: true
    subagent_enabled: true
    recursion_limit: 160
ModeThinkingPlanningSub-agents
flash———
thinking✓——
pro✓✓—
ultra✓✓✓
uv run cli agents run "Research Assistant" --mode ultra --chat
uv run cli agents run "Research Assistant" --sandbox docker "Explain QKD"
uv run cli agents tui "Research Assistant" --continue

Install with the harnessing extra; DEER_FLOW_PATH and cli init --deer-flow are no longer needed. Global DeerFlow settings go under a top-level deerflow: key (see config/examples/deerflow.yaml). From Python, use create_harness("Research Assistant") rather than the low-level EmbeddedDeerFlowClient.

Trajectories and Monitoring

Every deep-agent run is recorded in an ATOF trajectory store under <data_root>/trajectories/ (scope tree, tool args and results, skill loads, token usage).

uv run cli trajectory list
uv run cli trajectory tui                # interactive step-by-step replay
uv run cli trajectory show <id>
uv run cli trajectory diff <a> <b>
uv run cli trajectory stats
uv run cli trajectory prune

uv run cli monitoring status             # LangSmith / Langfuse / OTLP / local backends
uv run cli monitoring start              # self-hosted Langfuse (Docker)
uv run cli agents run research "..." --trace

Tracing backends are configured under monitoring.backends (see config/examples/monitoring.yaml); Langfuse needs the monitoring extra.

documents.label: BAML Structured Extraction — references/baml-structured.md
documents.html:
BAML Structured Extraction — references/baml-structured.md

BAML is a DSL for typed LLM functions. genai-tk uses it for structured extraction: a prompt that returns a validated Pydantic object instead of free text. The toolkit adds config-driven client loading, LLM routing through its own model IDs, manifest-based incremental batch runs, and Prefect flows that plug into the workflow engine.

Install the baml extra first, for example uv add "genai-tk[baml] @ git+https://github.com/tclatos/genai-tk@main". It pins baml-py, which also ships baml-cli.

Reach for BAML instead of LangChain's with_structured_output when the schema should be versioned and type-checked outside Python, or when you batch-extract from many Markdown or PDF files. The cost is a baml-cli generate step.

Concept Map

ConceptWhat it is
.baml fileTyped function: function ExtractResume(cv: string) -> Resume
BAML clientPackage generated by baml-cli generate with types and async_client (exposing b) modules
Config nameEntry under structured.<name> pointing at the client package (default unless --config)
cli baml runRun one function on one text input (delegates to the baml_run workflow)
cli baml extractBatch-process a directory of Markdown/PDF files (delegates to the baml_extract workflow)
baml_invokeLow-level async call with LLM override
BamlStructuredProcessorBatch extraction with KV-store caching

Setup

1. Write .baml definitions

// baml_src/extract.baml
class Experience {
  company string
  role    string
  years   int
}

class Resume {
  name       string
  skills     string[]
  experience Experience[]
}

function ExtractResume(cv: string) -> Resume {
  client GPT4o
  prompt #"
    Extract structured resume data from the following text:
    {{ cv }}
    {{ ctx.output_format }}
  "#
}

Functions that take a pdf parameter receive PDF files natively from cli baml extract.

2. Generate the client

uv run baml-cli generate          # from the directory holding baml_src/
# → baml_client/types.py, baml_client/async_client.py, ...

Regenerate after every .baml change. If baml-py and the generated client disagree on version, loading raises BamlVersionMismatchError; align the generator version in baml_src/generators.baml with the installed baml-py.

3. Point a config name at the package

# any merged config file, e.g. config/app_conf.yaml or a file pulled in by :merge
structured:
  default:
    baml_client: baml_client          # importable package (must expose .types and .async_client.b)
  legal:
    baml_client: myapp.legal_baml_client

baml_client is the only key (StructuredConfig). Check it imports: uv run python -c "import baml_client".

4. LLM routing

The client in the .baml file is a fallback. When you pass an LLM (--llm, llm=), genai-tk resolves it with LlmFactory and builds a BAML ClientRegistry (create_baml_client_registry). llm="default" resolves the configured default model; llm=None keeps the client declared in the .baml file.

from genai_tk.extra.structured.baml_util import create_baml_client_registry

registry = create_baml_client_registry("gpt-4o-mini@openai")   # options built from the LangChain model

Only models that resolve to ChatOpenAI are supported: OpenAI itself, plus any OpenAI-compatible base URL (OpenRouter, vLLM, LiteLLM, and so on), which map to BAML's openai-generic provider. Other providers raise ValueError: Provider not (yet?) supported for BAML.

BAML's own logging is set to ERROR unless you export BAML_LOG=debug|info|trace.

CLI

cli baml run — one input

uv run cli baml run ExtractResume -i "John Smith; 10 years Python, ML"
cat resume.txt | uv run cli baml run ExtractResume                     # stdin
uv run cli baml run ExtractResume -i "..." --config legal --llm gpt-4o-mini@openai
uv run cli baml run ExtractResume -i "..." --out-dir ./output --out-file john.json
uv run cli baml run ExtractResume -i "..." --out-dir '${paths.data_root}' --out-file john.json --force
OptionDefaultNotes
FUNCTION_NAMErequiredCase-sensitive BAML function name
--input, -istdinText input
--configdefaultKey under structured:
--llmclient defaultModel ID or tag
--out-dir, --out-filestdoutMust be given together; the file must end in .json
--forcefalseRecompute even if the manifest has this input

With an output, the result goes to <out-dir>/<ReturnTypeName>/<out-file> and a manifest skips repeated inputs. Without one, pretty JSON is printed to stdout.

cli baml extract — a directory

uv run cli baml extract ./docs ./output --function ExtractResume
uv run cli baml extract ./scans ./output --function ExtractDeliveryNote -p '**/*.pdf'
uv run cli baml extract ./reports ./output --function ExtractResume \
    -p '**/*.md' -p '!**/*_draft.md' --batch-size 10 --force
uv run cli baml extract '${paths.data_root}/reviews' '${paths.data_root}/structured' --function ExtractRainbow
OptionDefaultNotes
BASE_DIR, OUTPUT_DIRrequiredPositional; ${paths.*} interpolation works (single-quote it)
--functionrequiredBAML function name
--pathspec, -p**/*.mdGitwildmatch, repeatable, ! prefix excludes; this replaces the old --recursive/--include/--exclude
--batch-size5Files processed concurrently per batch
--configdefaultKey under structured:
--llmdefaultModel ID or tag
--forcefalseIgnore the manifest

Only .md, .markdown, and .pdf files are processed; PDFs are passed as baml_py.Pdf. Each output lands at <OUTPUT_DIR>/<ReturnTypeName>/<relative/source/path>.json, keeping the source tree layout.

Incremental runs

OUTPUT_DIR/manifest.json records, per source path, the content hash, the output path, and a schema fingerprint (prompt_fingerprint, a hash of the rendered output schema from baml_src/). A file is skipped when both its content and the schema are unchanged. Use --force once after prompt-only changes, because the fingerprint covers the output schema, not the prompt text. Delete manifest.json to start over.

Workflows and Prefect

Both CLI commands resolve the bundled baml_run / baml_extract workflows (see workflows.md), so BAML steps can compose into pipelines. The bundled baml_to_table pipeline extracts and then calls json_to_table to write CSV or Excel.

Known upstream mismatch (commit 7fbd7a3). The bundled baml_extract workflow declares sources, json_output_dir, and cache_dir, but cli baml extract sends base_dir/output_dir and the flow only accepts base_dir/output_dir. Expect missing required parameter 'sources' from cli baml extract, or unexpected argument(s) from baml_to_table. The baml_run workflow also does not forward --out-dir/ --out-file to its flow. Until upstream fixes the YAML, either override the workflow in your own workflows: config with matching parameter names, or call the flows directly:

from genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.baml_flow import (
    baml_single_input_flow,
    baml_structured_extraction_flow,
)

manifest = baml_structured_extraction_flow(
    "./docs",
    "./output",
    function_name="ExtractResume",
    pathspecs=["**/*.md", "!**/drafts/**"],
    batch_size=10,
    llm="gpt-4o-mini@openai",
)
print(manifest.model_name, len(manifest.entries))

result, model_name, resolved_llm, rel_path = baml_single_input_flow(
    "John Smith; SW engineer", "ExtractResume", output_dir="./output", output_file="john.json"
)

The flows run under Prefect's ConcurrentTaskRunner; see workflows.md for ephemeral versus server mode.

Programmatic API

baml_invoke

import asyncio

from genai_tk.extra.structured.baml_util import baml_invoke

resume = asyncio.run(
    baml_invoke(
        "ExtractResume",
        {"__input__": "John Smith; SW engineer, 10 yrs"},   # __input__ maps to the first parameter
        config_name="default",
        llm="gpt-4o-mini@openai",
    )
)
print(resume.name, resume.skills)
  • Signature: baml_invoke(function_name, params, config_name="default", llm="default", check_result_is_pydantic=False). The argument is params, not inputs.
  • Multi-parameter functions take real names: {"contract": text, "jurisdiction": "FR"}.
  • If a parameter is typed as a BAML class and you pass a str, it raises TypeError with a hint.
  • Calls are wrapped in a NeMo Relay scope when nemo_relay is installed, so they appear in trajectories.
  • It does not stream. For streaming, call b.ExtractResume.stream(...) from the generated client and pass baml_options={"client_registry": create_baml_client_registry(...)} yourself.

BamlStructuredProcessor

import asyncio

from baml_client import b
from baml_client.types import Resume
from genai_tk.extra.structured.baml_processor import BamlStructuredProcessor

processor = BamlStructuredProcessor[Resume](model_cls=Resume, baml_function=b.ExtractResume)
results = asyncio.run(processor.abatch_analyze_documents(["a", "b"], [text_a, text_b]))

by_name = BamlStructuredProcessor[Resume](
    function_name="ExtractResume",       # goes through baml_invoke, so llm= routing applies
    llm="gpt-4o-mini@openai",
    config_name="default",
    kvstore_id="default",                # key in the kv_store: config section
    force=False,
)
one = by_name.analyze_document("cv-42", markdown)          # sync helper
FieldDefaultNotes
model_clsNoneDeduced from the first result if omitted, but then the cache is skipped for that batch
baml_functionNoneGenerated async method; bypasses genai-tk LLM routing
function_nameNoneUse with llm= / config_name=; one of the two is required
config_namedefaultKey under structured:
llmNoneModel ID; only used with function_name
kvstore_iddefaultCache store; falsy disables caching
forcefalseSkip cache reads

Cached documents are loaded by ID, the rest run concurrently with asyncio.gather, and successes are saved back. Failures are logged and dropped from the result list rather than raised, so compare lengths when every document matters. await processor.process_files(paths) uses each file's stem as its ID.

Errors

All live in genai_tk.extra.structured.exceptions and subclass StructuredOutputError:

ExceptionCause
ValueError "BAML client package not found in config"No structured.<config_name> entry
BamlClientLoadErrorPackage, .types, or .async_client.b not importable
BamlVersionMismatchErrorGenerated client and installed baml-py versions differ
BamlFunctionNotFoundErrorFunction name not in the client (case-sensitive; regenerate)
BamlInvocationErrorReturn type could not be validated as Pydantic

Anti-Patterns

  • Passing inputs= to baml_invoke, or --recursive/--include/--exclude to cli baml extract: these are the old API. Use params and -p pathspecs.
  • Importing genai_tk.extra.structured.baml_prefect_flow: it moved to genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.baml_flow.
  • Using an Anthropic or Gemini native model ID with --llm: route it through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as OpenRouter, or keep the client declared in the .baml file (llm=None).
  • Forgetting baml-cli generate after editing .baml: the old client keeps running the old schema.
  • Expecting baml_function= to honor llm=: only the function_name path routes through genai-tk.

documents.label: CLI, Install & Project Init — references/cli-and-init.md
documents.html:
CLI, Install & Project Init — references/cli-and-init.md

The cli entry point (genai_tk.main.cli:main) is a Typer app whose command groups are declared in config/app_conf.yaml under cli.commands and resolved by dotted path. A project extends the CLI by adding one class and one YAML line.

Installation

genai-tk is not published on PyPI. Install it from git with uv; Python >=3.12 is required.

uv add "genai-tk @ git+https://github.com/tclatos/genai-tk@main"
uv add "genai-tk[harnessing,browser] @ git+https://github.com/tclatos/genai-tk@main"   # with extras
uv add --editable /path/to/genai-tk                                                  # local clone

Extras

ExtraBrings inNeeded for
harnessingdeepagents>=0.7.13, agent-sandbox, opensandbox, opensandbox-server, deerflow-harness[tui] (pinned commit)type: deep, DeerFlow, Docker sandbox
browserplaywrightDirect (host) browser tools
nlpspaCy + en_core_web_md, Presidio, langchain-huggingfacePII anonymization, spaCy BM25, cross-encoder rerank
postgreslangchain-postgres, psycopgPgVector, pg_hybrid retriever
streamlitstreamlit, streamlit-monacojust webapp
bamlbaml-py==0.223.0BAML structured extraction
chromadbchromadb, langchain-chromaChroma vector store
doclingdocling, easyocrDocling converter in markdownize
monitoringlangfuse, OpenTelemetry SDK/OTLP exporter, openinferenceLangfuse / OTLP tracing
allEvery extra above except monitoring—

Core already includes Prefect, prefect-yaml, LangSmith, NeMo Relay, mcp>=2.0, MarkItDown, and FastEmbed. dev and evals are dependency groups for contributors, not extras.

Feature-gated code calls genai_tk.config_mgmt.features.require_feature("<name>"); install a missing feature later with uv sync --extra <name>.

Do not use [tool.uv] override-dependencies on genai-tk in a downstream project: it strips forwarded extras. Pin sibling checkouts with [tool.uv.sources] instead.

cli init — Scaffold a Project

uv init my-app && cd my-app
uv add "genai-tk @ git+https://github.com/tclatos/genai-tk@main"
uv run cli init --name "My Agent App"
uv run cli init --extra harnessing --extra browser      # repeatable; runs uv sync --extra X
uv run cli init --with-graph --graph-path ../genai-graph # knowledge-graph + benchmark scaffolding
uv run cli init --force                                  # overwrite existing files

The only flags are --name/-n, --extra/-e, --with-graph/-g, --graph-path, and --force/-f. Upstream docs mention -t/--template presets, --minimal, and --with-deer-flow, but these are not implemented; the scaffolder always produces the agent-app layout.

init runs uv sync itself and removes the main.py stub that uv init creates.

What it generates

PathPurpose
config/Full default config tree (app_conf.yaml, providers/, agents.yaml, webapp.yaml, …)
justfilerun, sync, fmt, lint (ruff + cli skills validate --all), check, test, test-unit, skills, add-skill, webapp
<pkg>/commands/agent_commands.pyAgentCommands → cli agent list / cli agent chat (singular agent)
<pkg>/tools/example_tool.pyExample LangChain tool referenced from config/agents.yaml
<pkg>/webapp/pages/demos/hello_agent.py, <pkg>/main/streamlit.pyStreamlit demo page and entry point
skills/{runtime,development,governance,vendor,custom,community}/Bundled upstream skills + custom/getting-started/SKILL.md
AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, docs/SKILLS.md, docs/EXTENDING.mdCoding-agent guidance
pyproject.tomlPinned to Python >=3.12,<3.13, hatchling build backend, [tool.uv] package = true, forwarded extras

It also patches app_conf.yaml (cli.commands gets <pkg>.commands.agent_commands.AgentCommands) and webapp.yaml (pages and navigation). just run maps to uv run cli agent chat.

Command Tree

Run uv run cli (no arguments) or uv run cli --help for the live tree. As of 7fbd7a3:

GroupSubcommands
initflags above
infoconfig, config-keys [KEY], doctor [--fix], models, llm-profile ID [--reload], mcp-tools, commands, ls
corellm, embedd, similarity, mcp-call, classifier
agentsrun [PROFILE] [QUERY], list, tui PROFILE (DeerFlow only)
sandboxstart, stop, status, list, pull
mcpserverstart, serve, list, generate (--name, `--transport stdio\sse\streamable-http, --host, --port`)
ragadd-files, query, embed, delete, info, list-retrievers, list-configs
workflowrun, list, show, validate, serve
prefectstart, stop, status, ui
bamlrun, extract
skillslist, add, create, validate, info, search
trajectorylist, show, open, link, tui, tail, replay, export, diff, skills, stats, prune, view
monitoringstatus, start, stop, test, open, tail, clear
toolsgpt-researcher, browser-agent
testunit, fast_integration, full_integration, all, evals, select, notebooks

Frequently used invocations:

uv run cli core llm -i "tell me a joke" -m parrot_local@fake      # prompt via -i or stdin, not positional
echo "hello" | uv run cli core llm -m gpt-4o-mini@openai --stream
uv run cli agents run research "Explain async generators"          # profile is positional
uv run cli agents run research --chat --thread-id t1
uv run cli agents run research "..." --json                        # NDJSON event stream
uv run cli info doctor --fix

Global flag --logging takes no value; it forces TRACE-level logs.

The loader only imports modules whose dotted path contains the invoked group name, so a broken optional command module does not break unrelated groups. An unresolvable entry in cli.commands only logs a warning.

Extending the CLI — CliTopCommand

# my_pkg/commands/report_commands.py
import typer

from genai_tk.cli.base import CliTopCommand


class ReportCommands(CliTopCommand):
    """Report generation commands."""

    def get_description(self) -> tuple[str, str]:
        return "report", "Generate reports from project data."

    def register_sub_commands(self, cli_app: typer.Typer) -> None:
        @cli_app.command("weekly")
        def weekly(
            week: str = typer.Argument(..., help="ISO week, e.g. 2026-W41"),
            llm: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--llm", "-m"),
        ) -> None:
            """Write the weekly report."""
            from my_pkg.reports import build_weekly  # import heavy deps inside the command

            build_weekly(week, llm=llm)
# config/app_conf.yaml
cli:
  commands:
    - genai_tk.cli.commands_core.CoreCommands
    - genai_tk.cli.commands_info.InfoCommands
    # ...keep the existing entries...
    - my_pkg.commands.report_commands.ReportCommands

Contract:

  • CliTopCommand is a Pydantic BaseModel + ABC; implement get_description() -> (name, help) and register_sub_commands(app). register() is inherited.
  • Entries must be dotted paths (pkg.module.Class). The module:Class form fails validation even though an upstream docstring shows it.
  • Classes are instantiated with no arguments; entries cannot carry kwargs. A plain function entry is called as fn(cli_app).
  • Use a real importable package path (my_pkg...), not src.my_pkg..., unless src is itself a package.

Then run uv run cli report weekly 2026-W41.

Skills Manager — cli skills

Upstream organizes SKILL.md files (skills.sh format) in tiers:

TierPurpose
skills/runtime/Used by agents during runs (codeact, browser-automation, query-writing, …)
skills/development/Recipes for extending the toolkit (agent-profiles, add-tool, rag-systems, …)
skills/governance/Standards and audits (repo-map, evaluation-testing, pii-anonymization)
skills/vendor/Imported third-party skills, not edited directly
skills/custom/, skills/community/Project-specific and community-installed skills
uv run cli skills list --source custom
uv run cli skills create invoice-review               # scaffold a skills.sh-format SKILL.md
uv run cli skills add --skillssh langchain-ai/langchain-skills
uv run cli skills add --git https://github.com/org/repo --path skills/foo
uv run cli skills validate --all

After cli init, a project's skills/development/ folder contains upstream's own recipes (agent-profiles, add-tool, add-cli-command, rag-systems, workflow-engine, …). They are useful deep dives, but some lag the code (for example development/configuration still references utils/config_mngr.py), so check imports against the installed package.

House Conventions for Code in genai-tk Projects

From upstream AGENTS.md:

  • Python 3.12+ typing (str | None, list[str]); avoid Any (use discriminated unions, TypeAlias)
  • Absolute imports; ruff, line length 120; PascalCase classes, snake_case functions, _private
  • Pydantic v2 for structured data: model_config = {...}, model_post_init(), model_dump_json()
  • loguru for logging; Google-style docstrings, no types, no Raises:, no field docstrings
  • Config via typed models: global_config().section(key, Model) / .section_dict(key, Model)
  • Tests: pytest style, fake_llm_id / fake_llm / fake_embeddings fixtures, fake providers over mocks, markers unit, integration, fake_models, real_models; never call get_pytest_config() at module level and never name fixtures pytest_*
  • Keep system prompts in YAML (system_prompt:), domain knowledge in SKILL.md
  • Upstream rule for its own repo: update matching skills, docs, and CHANGELOG.md in the same commit

Repo Recipes (upstream justfile)

For contributors working in a clone of genai-tk:

just install-dev        # uv sync with dev deps
just check              # fmt + lint + test
just test-unit
just new ../my-app      # uv init --bare + uv add + cli init + uv sync + smoke test
just lint-skills

Downstream projects can import the shared tk.just recipes (set pkg_name first). Docker images are built via deploy/docker.just (just docker-build, EXTRAS=...).

documents.label: Configuration — references/configuration.md
documents.html:
Configuration — references/configuration.md

genai-tk uses OmegaConf with a few custom directives. Everything the toolkit builds (models, agents, retrievers, workflows, CLI groups, webapp pages) is read from this merged config.

Imports

from genai_tk.config_mgmt.config_mngr import (
    global_config,         # singleton OmegaConfig
    global_config_reload,
    switch_profile,        # set GENAITK_PROFILE and reload
    use_active_context,    # apply a named overlay without reloading
    get_raw_config,        # underlying DictConfig
    paths_config,
    ImportResolver,        # dotted-path resolver behind the IoC registry
)

The old genai_tk.utils.config_mngr module no longer exists and there is no compatibility shim.

Discovery and Loading

  • The root file is config/app_conf.yaml, looked up relative to the current working directory. The loader does not walk up parent directories (upstream docs claim it does). If neither path exists, ConfigFileNotFoundError is raised; run from the project root or cli init first.
  • load_dotenv() runs on import, so .env in the CWD is loaded. The cli entry point also loads ~/.env.
  • ${oc.env:VAR,default} reads environment variables; standard OmegaConf interpolation (${paths.project}) works across merged files.

app_conf.yaml Anatomy

profile: ${oc.env:GENAITK_PROFILE,local}      # active profile name

paths:
  home: ${oc.env:HOME}
  project: ${oc.env:PWD}
  config: ${paths.project}/config
  data_root: ${paths.project}/data

:merge:                                        # gitignore-style patterns, relative to config/
  - "**/*.yaml"
  - "!demos/**"
  - "!mcp/**"
  - "!examples/agents/**"

:profiles:                                     # inline overlays; the active one is applied last
  local:
    llm:
      models:
        default: gpt-4o-mini@openai
        fast_model: claude-haiku@openrouter
        fake: parrot_local@fake
      cache: sqlite
      cache_path: data/llm_cache/langchain.db
    embeddings:
      models: {default: embeddings_768@fake}
  production:
    :merge: ["prod/**/*.yaml"]                 # an overlay may pull in extra files
    llm: {models: {default: claude-haiku@openrouter}}
  pytest:
    llm: {models: {default: parrot_local@fake}}

:env:                                          # exported to os.environ at load time
  LOGURU_LEVEL: INFO
  LANGSMITH_TRACING: "false"

cli:
  commands:
    - genai_tk.cli.commands_core.CoreCommands
    - genai_tk.cli.commands_info.InfoCommands
    # ...

Directive semantics

DirectiveBehavior
profile:Active profile. Resolution: GENAITK_PROFILE env var → profile: key → legacy default_config: → local
:merge:Patterns are expanded with rglob under config/, sorted, then deep-merged in order (later wins). !pattern excludes
:profiles:Map of overlays. The active profile's block is merged after all :merge: files and may contain its own :merge:
:env:Sets environment variables. It overwrites variables that are already set (upstream docs say otherwise)

What changed from older genai-tk versions:

OldNow
baseline.yaml, overrides.yamlInline :profiles: blocks
default_config: ${oc.env:BLUEPRINT_CONFIG,baseline}profile: ${oc.env:GENAITK_PROFILE,local}
Explicit file list in :merge:Glob patterns with ! excludes
cfg.select_config("prod")switch_profile("prod") (reload) or use_active_context("prod") (overlay)
llm.default, llm.tags.*llm.models.default, llm.models.<tag>
genai_tk.core.commands_core.CoreCommandsgenai_tk.cli.commands_core.CoreCommands

Reading Config

from pydantic import BaseModel

from genai_tk.config_mgmt.config_mngr import global_config


class ReportConfig(BaseModel):
    output_dir: str = "data/reports"
    max_items: int = 50


cfg = global_config()

cfg.get("llm.models.default")                         # Any
cfg.get_str("llm.models.default")
cfg.get_bool("prefect.auto_start")
cfg.get_list("cli.commands")
cfg.get_dict("retrievers")
cfg.get_dir_path("paths.data_root", create_if_not_exists=True)   # Path
cfg.get_dsn("postgres.default.url", driver="asyncpg")            # SQLAlchemy URL

report = cfg.section("report", ReportConfig)                     # typed; empty/default model if missing
stores = cfg.section_dict("embeddings_store", StoreConfig)       # dict[str, StoreConfig]; injects name

Upstream's convention is to read every top-level key through a typed Pydantic model with section() / section_dict(). Both return an empty result instead of raising when the key is absent. section_dict accepts an Annotated[..., Field(discriminator=...)] union.

Mutating at runtime

cfg.set("llm.models.default", "parrot_local@fake")    # in-memory only
cfg.merge_yaml("""
retrievers:
  scratch: {type: genai_tk.core.retrievers.VectorRetriever, embeddings_store: memory}
""")                                                  # raw YAML string or a file path
cfg.use_context("production")                         # apply a top-level overlay key

Switching profiles

GENAITK_PROFILE=production uv run cli agents run research "..."
from genai_tk.config_mgmt.config_mngr import switch_profile

switch_profile("pytest")    # sets GENAITK_PROFILE and reloads the singleton

In tests, upstream switches to the pytest profile in a session-scoped autouse fixture; read test settings with genai_tk.config_mgmt.test_config.get_pytest_config() inside fixtures, never at module level.

Introspection

uv run cli info config                 # resolved config + API-key status per provider
uv run cli info config-keys            # which file each top-level key came from
uv run cli info config-keys llm
uv run cli info doctor --fix           # environment pre-flight checks

cfg.config_keys_info() returns the same provenance map in Python.

Inversion of Control — ImportResolver

Config values that name code are fully qualified dotted paths resolved with ImportResolver.import_from_qualified("pkg.module.Object"). The resolver tries progressively shorter module prefixes, so pkg.module.Class.method-style paths work. A bare name without dots triggers a slower AST scan of the project and is fragile; always write the full path.

The same mechanism resolves:

Config locationWhat it names
providers.<name>.chat_class / embeddings_class / decision_classProvider implementation classes
cli.commands[]CliTopCommand subclasses or fn(cli_app) callables
agents.<key>.tools[], middlewares[].classTool factories and middleware classes
retrievers.<tag>.type, embeddings_store.<tag>.backendRetriever builders and vector backends
workflows.<name>.runPrefect flows or other workflows
markdownize_converters.<name>.classDocument converters
ui.navigationStreamlit pages, including genai_tk://demos/agent.py library resources

To extend the toolkit, write a class in your package and reference it from YAML; do not fork the library.

Typical File Layout After cli init

config/
├── app_conf.yaml          # root: profile, paths, :merge, :profiles, :env, cli.commands
├── agents.yaml            # agents: + agent_defaults:
├── providers/
│   ├── providers.yaml     # provider registry (chat_class, api_key_env_var, api_base, ...)
│   ├── llm.yaml           # llm.exceptions: models not covered by models.dev
│   ├── embeddings.yaml    # embeddings.registry
│   └── decision_models.yaml
├── mcp_servers.yaml       # mcpServers: / mcpProjectServers:
├── webapp.yaml
└── examples/              # bundled examples (agents/, rag.yaml, workflows.yaml, ...)

Because :merge: globs **/*.yaml, any new YAML file you drop under config/ is picked up automatically unless an exclude pattern matches it. Keep keys unique across files: later files silently override earlier ones.

Network Proxies

Corporate proxies are honored through the standard HTTP(S)_PROXY variables. Hosts that must bypass the proxy (local vLLM, Ollama, sandbox) go under net.proxy_bypass_hosts; they are added to NO_PROXY at load time.

documents.label: Models, Providers & Decision Models — references/models.md
documents.html:
Models, Providers & Decision Models — references/models.md

genai-tk resolves every model through one identifier format, model_id@provider, and one provider registry (config/providers/providers.yaml). The factories return plain LangChain objects.

Imports

from genai_tk.core.factories import (
    get_llm,
    get_embeddings,
    get_decision_model,
    get_decision_model_from_chat_model,
    LlmFactory,
    EmbeddingsFactory,
)

Module paths: genai_tk.core.factories.llm_factory, genai_tk.core.factories.embeddings_factory, genai_tk.core.factories.decision_model_factory. The old genai_tk.core.llm_factory and genai_tk.core.embeddings_factory modules are gone with no shims.

get_llm

get_llm(
    llm: str = "default",          # tag, model_id@provider, or "model (effort)@provider[:routing]"
    json_mode: bool = False,
    streaming: bool = False,
    reasoning: bool | None = None, # legacy bool; prefer inline effort or reasoning_effort=
    cache: str | None = None,      # "memory" | "sqlite" | "no_cache"; None = LangChain global cache
    routing: str | None = None,
    provider_routing: dict | None = None,
    **kwargs,                      # forwarded to the chat model (temperature, max_tokens, ...)
) -> BaseChatModel
llm = get_llm()                                   # llm.models.default of the active profile
llm = get_llm("fast_model")                       # any tag under llm.models
llm = get_llm("gpt-4o-mini@openai")
llm = get_llm("parrot_local@fake")                # echoes input; no key needed
llm = get_llm("gpt-4o-mini@openai", temperature=0.7, streaming=True)
llm = get_llm("gpt-4o-mini@openai", json_mode=True, cache="sqlite")

Defaults applied by the factory: temperature=0.0, seed=42, max_retries=2. If the provider's API-key variable is empty, get_llm raises EnvironmentError instead of failing on the first call.

llm_id= and llm_tag= are deprecated and only warn; pass the identifier as llm.

Reasoning effort

llm = get_llm("o3 (high)@openai")                         # inline effort
llm = get_llm("claude-haiku (low)@openrouter")
llm = get_llm("o3@openai", reasoning_effort="medium")     # flat kwarg form
llm = get_llm("o3@openai", reasoning_max_tokens=4000)

Valid efforts: low, medium, high, minimal, xhigh, max, none (none disables reasoning). Anything else raises ValueError. Provider mixins translate the effort into each API's payload.

Do not pass reasoning={...} to get_llm: the reasoning: bool | None parameter captures the dict and validation fails (upstream docs/core.md shows this broken form). For a raw reasoning dict use LlmFactory(llm=..., llm_params={"reasoning": {...}}).

Gateway routing

On openrouter, edenai, and edenai-eur, append a strategy to the identifier or tag:

llm = get_llm("claude-haiku@openrouter:speed")    # speed | cost | latency | exact
llm = get_llm("fast_model:cost")

The suffix is ignored for other providers.

Identifier resolution

model_id@provider contains exactly one @. Resolution order:

  1. Exact known identifier (from llm.exceptions or the models.dev catalog)
  2. A tag under llm.models
  3. Hyphen/underscore normalization (gpt_4o_mini ↔ gpt-4o-mini)
  4. Fuzzy match against models.dev; auto-selected when the score is ≥ 0.8

Fuzzy matching makes bare names work interactively, but in YAML and code always write the full identifier so a catalog update cannot change which model you get.

The models.dev catalog (1000+ models, capabilities, context windows) is cached at data/models_dev.json under the CWD and fetched when missing. Refresh it with uv run cli info llm-profile <id> --reload.

Declaring Models — llm.exceptions

Most models need no declaration because models.dev covers them. Use config/providers/llm.yaml for models that are missing from the catalog, need aliases, or need capability overrides:

llm:
  exceptions:
    - model_id: parrot_local
      providers:
        - fake: parrot

    - model_id: claude-haiku                       # one alias, two providers
      providers:
        - openrouter: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
        - edenai: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5

    - model_id: ministral_8b
      providers:
        - openrouter: mistralai/ministral-8b-latest
      capabilities: ['structured_outputs']         # thinking | structured_outputs | pdf | vision
      max_tokens: 4096
      context_window: 32768

Each entry under providers: creates a separate identifier (claude-haiku@openrouter, claude-haiku@edenai). The list is not a fallback chain; upstream docs/llm-selection.md describes it as one, which is wrong.

Tags (what get_llm("fast_model") resolves) live under llm.models in a profile block of app_conf.yaml:

:profiles:
  local:
    llm:
      models:
        default: gpt-4o-mini@openai
        fast_model: claude-haiku@openrouter
        default_vlm: gemini-2.5-flash@openrouter
        fake: parrot_local@fake

Embeddings

get_embeddings(
    embeddings: str = "default",
    encoding_str: str | None = None,     # prefix for documents (e.g. "passage: ")
    retrieving_str: str | None = None,   # prefix for queries (e.g. "query: ")
    cache_embeddings: bool = False,
) -> Embeddings
emb = get_embeddings()                          # embeddings.models.default
emb = get_embeddings("embeddings_768@fake")     # offline fake
vectors = emb.embed_documents(["doc 1", "doc 2"])

Defaults and tags live under embeddings.models; extra models go under embeddings.registry in config/providers/embeddings.yaml (entries can set dimension). embeddings_id= / embeddings_tag= are deprecated.

Providers — providers.yaml

Each provider entry names its implementation classes by dotted path (resolved via ImportResolver):

FieldPurpose
chat_class / embeddings_class / decision_classImplementation per role (legacy use: = chat_class)
api_key_env_varEnv var checked before construction
api_baseBase URL for OpenAI-compatible or self-hosted endpoints
litellm_prefix, gateway, extra_body, custom_headers, special_env_varsProvider-specific wiring
openai_compatible, seed_param_locationBehavior flags used by the mixins

Bundled providers include openai, anthropic, google, mistral, groq, deepinfra, edenai, edenai-eur, openrouter, github, azure, together, deepseek, huggingface, ollama, vllm, litellm, custom, fake, local (FastEmbed, embeddings only), and laya (decision models only). A labs: section maps models to the lab that trained them.

Chat classes live in genai_tk.core.providers.chat (OpenAIChat, OpenRouterChat, EdenAIChat, GroqChat, VllmChat, OllamaChat, MistralChat, AzureChat, LiteLLMChat, FakeChat, …) and compose mixins from genai_tk.core.providers.mixins: SeedHandlingMixin, ReasoningMixin, OpenRouterRoutingMixin, EdenAIRoutingMixin, EdenAIReasoningMixin. If a class exposes a create() classmethod, the factory calls it with only the kwargs its signature accepts.

On-prem models (vLLM, Ollama)

Override api_base on an existing provider rather than inventing a new provider key. Some lookups still read only the bundled provider list, so a brand-new key can fail with "Unknown provider".

# config/providers/providers.yaml (project override)
providers:
  vllm:
    api_base: http://gpu-box.internal:8000/v1
  ollama:
    api_base: http://localhost:11434
# config/providers/llm.yaml — self-hosted models are not in models.dev, so declare them
llm:
  exceptions:
    - model_id: qwen3_8b
      providers:
        - vllm: Qwen/Qwen3-8B          # the model name served by vLLM
export VLLM_API_KEY=anything     # vLLM requires the variable to be non-empty
llm = get_llm("qwen3_8b@vllm")   # undeclared ids raise "Unknown LLM"

The - custom: {model, base_url, default_headers} dict form in llm.exceptions parses, but base_url and headers are not currently forwarded to the client, so prefer the api_base override.

Caching

llm.cache (memory | sqlite | no_cache) and llm.cache_path set the global LangChain cache; get_llm(..., cache=...) overrides per model. genai_tk.core.cache.LlmCache.set_method() changes it at runtime. in_memory and redis are not valid values.

Decision Models (System 1)

Decision models are fast, non-autoregressive classifiers (OpenRouter Clef/Jev, EdenAI, Laya ModernBERT, OpenAI, and an offline fake) for routing, scoring, and guard checks in well under a second.

from genai_tk.core.decision_models import Choice, ClassifierRequest, Noul, Score
from genai_tk.core.factories import get_decision_model

model = get_decision_model()                    # decision.models.default
request = ClassifierRequest(
    state="Customer: my card was charged twice for order 1042.",
    questions={
        "is_complaint": Noul(instructions="Is the customer complaining?"),
        "topic": Choice(
            instructions="What is the main topic?",
            criteria={"billing": "Payments, charges, refunds", "shipping": "Delivery issues", "other": "Anything else"},
        ),
        "urgency": Score(instructions="How urgent is this?", criteria=["low", "medium", "high"]),
    },
)
response = model.invoke(request)
response.nouls["is_complaint"].noul       # probability in [0, 1]
response.choices["topic"].choice          # plus .confidence and .probabilities
response.scores["urgency"].score          # plus .legend and .probabilities
  • Noul returns a calibrated probability; Choice takes a criteria dict (at least one key); Score takes a criteria list of at least two ordered levels.
  • state accepts a string, a dict, a LangChain message, or a list of messages.
  • BaseDecisionModel is a LangChain Runnable: invoke, ainvoke, batch_invoke, abatch_invoke (auto-chunks by the model's max_questions), plus decide_noul, decide_choice, decide_score helpers.
  • get_decision_model_from_chat_model(llm=...) wraps a regular chat model when no decision backend is available.
  • Tags live under decision.models (default, fast, accurate, fake); registry entries under decision_models.registry with context_length, max_questions, description.
uv run cli core classifier --demo
uv run cli core classifier --noul "Is this spam?" -s "Win a free cruise now!!!"
uv run cli core classifier --choice "Topic?" -c "billing:Payments, shipping:Delivery" -s "Where is my parcel?"
uv run cli core classifier --score "Urgency?" -c "low,medium,high" -s "Server is down" -m fake

The CLI command is classifier; upstream docs that say cli core decision are out of date.

CLI Cheatsheet

uv run cli info models                        # everything resolvable
uv run cli info llm-profile gpt-4o-mini@openai
uv run cli info config                        # API-key status per provider
uv run cli core llm -i "hello" -m parrot_local@fake
uv run cli core llm -i "solve 17*23" -m "o3 (low)@openai" --reasoning
uv run cli core embedd "some text" -m default
uv run cli core similarity "reference sentence" "candidate one" "candidate two"
