documents.html:
RAG — references/rag.md

genai-tk's retrieval layer separates where vectors live (embeddings_store:), how to search (retrievers:), and how documents are split (chunkers:). All three are YAML-declared and resolved by fully qualified class paths.

Imports

from genai_tk.core.factories import ChunkerFactory, ManagedRetriever, RetrieverFactory
from genai_tk.core.embeddings_store import EmbeddingsStore

The old genai_tk.core.retriever_factory, genai_tk.tools.langchain.rag_tool_factory, and genai_tk.extra.rag.* modules no longer exist.

Embeddings Stores

embeddings_store:
  in_memory:
    backend: genai_tk.core.vector_backends.InMemoryBackend
  scratch:
    backend: genai_tk.core.vector_backends.ChromaBackend
    embeddings: default                       # embeddings tag or model_id@provider
    config: {storage: "::memory::"}
  chroma:
    backend: genai_tk.core.vector_backends.ChromaBackend
    embeddings: default
    table_name_prefix: embeddings
    config: {storage: "${paths.data_root}/vector_store"}
  pg:
    backend: genai_tk.core.vector_backends.PgVectorBackend
    embeddings: default
    config:
      postgres: default                       # → postgres.default section
      postgres_schema: public
      hybrid_search: true

postgres:
  default:
    mode: external                            # external | pgembed
    url: ${oc.env:POSTGRES_URL}
Backendconfig: keysExtra
genai_tk.core.vector_backends.InMemoryBackendnonecore
genai_tk.core.vector_backends.ChromaBackendstorage (::memory:: or a path)chromadb
genai_tk.core.vector_backends.PgVectorBackendpostgres, postgres_schema, metadata_columns, hybrid_search, hybrid_search_configpostgres

Store-level fields: backend, embeddings, table_name_prefix, collection_metadata, config.

Short names (backend: Chroma, InMemory, PgVector) no longer resolve; always use the qualified class path. ZVec appears in upstream marketing but has no YAML backend class yet.

store = EmbeddingsStore.create_from_config("chroma")   # direct instantiation raises
vector_store = store.get_vector_store()                # LangChain VectorStore

Retrievers

retrievers:
  docs:
    type: genai_tk.core.retrievers.VectorRetriever
    embeddings_store: chroma
    top_k: 4
    record_manager_url: "sqlite:///${paths.data_root}/record_manager/docs.db"   # dedup on re-ingest

  docs_bm25:
    type: genai_tk.core.retrievers.BM25Retriever
    k: 4
    preprocessing: default                  # default | spacy (needs the nlp extra)

  hybrid:
    type: genai_tk.core.retrievers.EnsembleRetriever
    retrievers:
      - {ref: docs, weight: 0.7}
      - {ref: docs_bm25, weight: 0.3}       # weights are normalized

  best:
    type: genai_tk.core.retrievers.RerankedRetriever
    retriever: hybrid
    reranker: embeddings                    # embeddings | cohere | cross_encoder
    top_k: 3
typeFields
genai_tk.core.retrievers.VectorRetrieverembeddings_store (required), top_k=4, record_manager_url
genai_tk.core.retrievers.BM25Retrieverk=4, `preprocessing=default\spacy, spacy_model, cache_dir (default ${paths.data_root}/bm25_cache/<tag>), bm25_params`
genai_tk.core.retrievers.EnsembleRetrieverretrievers: [{ref, weight=0.5}] (reciprocal-rank fusion)
genai_tk.core.retrievers.RerankedRetrieverretriever (required), reranker, top_k=3, reranker_model, embeddings
genai_tk.core.retrievers.PgHybridRetrieverembeddings, postgres, schema_name, table_name_prefix, top_k, metadata_columns, hybrid_search=True, hybrid_search_config, record_manager_url
genai_tk.core.retrievers.ZeroEntropyRetrievercollection_name (required), k=5, retrieval_type (read-only, ZeroEntropy SDK)

Known quirks at 7fbd7a3:

  • type: vector / bm25 / ensemble short aliases do not resolve (the alias fallback is dead code).
  • fetch_k on RerankedRetriever and search_type on VectorRetriever are accepted but have no effect.
  • The automatic SQLite record manager for persistent stores no longer triggers; set record_manager_url explicitly if you re-ingest the same files.
  • The embeddings reranker is an EmbeddingsFilter (similarity threshold 0.7); cross_encoder needs langchain-huggingface (nlp extra); cohere needs a Cohere key.

ManagedRetriever

RetrieverFactory.create(tag) returns a ManagedRetriever, an async-first wrapper:

from langchain_core.documents import Document

from genai_tk.core.factories import RetrieverFactory

retriever = RetrieverFactory.create("docs")
await retriever.aadd_documents([Document(page_content="genai-tk is YAML-driven.", metadata={"src": "a.md"})])
docs = await retriever.aquery("What drives genai-tk?", k=5, filter={"src": "a.md"})
print(retriever.get_stats(), retriever.has_store)

RetrieverFactory.list_available_configs()     # all retriever tags
MethodNotes
aquery(query, k=None, filter=None) / queryk/filter only apply to vector- or BM25-backed retrievers
aadd_documents(docs) / add_documentsRaises RuntimeError when there is no writable store (has_store is false)
adelete_store() / delete_storeChroma and BM25 only; otherwise NotImplementedError
get_stats(), .retriever, .storeIntrospection; .retriever is the LangChain BaseRetriever

Ensemble and ZeroEntropy retrievers go through retriever.ainvoke(query), so k and filter are ignored. A reranked retriever exposes its base store, so aquery on it bypasses the reranker; call await retriever.retriever.ainvoke(query) when you need reranked results.

Ingest into the base retrievers (docs, docs_bm25); ensembles and rerankers read from them.

Chunkers

chunkers:
  recursive:
    class: langchain_text_splitters.RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
    params: {chunk_size: 512, chunk_overlap: 50}
  markdown:
    class: genai_tk.workflow.rag.chonkie_splitter.ChonkieTextSplitter
    params: {chunker_type: markdown, max_tokens: 300, min_tokens: 50, merge_small_chunks: true, encoding_name: o200k_base}
  auto_map:                     # extension → chunker; used by --chunker auto
    ".md": markdown
    ".txt": recursive
    ".default": recursive
from genai_tk.core.factories import ChunkerFactory

splitter = ChunkerFactory.create("markdown")
splitter = ChunkerFactory.create_for_file("notes/intro.md")    # chunker_name="auto" → auto_map
chunks = splitter.split_documents(docs)

CLI — cli rag

uv run cli rag list-retrievers
uv run cli rag list-configs
uv run cli rag add-files ./docs -r docs                          # base dir is positional
uv run cli rag add-files ./docs -r docs -p "**/*.md" -p "!drafts/**" --chunker markdown --dry-run
uv run cli rag add-files ./docs -r docs --force --batch-size 20 --chunk-size 512
uv run cli rag query "What drives genai-tk?" -r docs --k 5
uv run cli rag query "pricing" -r docs --filter '{"src": "a.md"}' --full
uv run cli rag embed docs -t "one-off text" -m '{"src": "cli"}'
uv run cli rag info docs
uv run cli rag delete docs -f
  • add-files BASE_DIR [-p/--pathspec ...] [-r/--retriever NAME] [-f/--force] [--dry-run] [-b/--batch-size 10] [--chunk-size 512] [--chunker auto]. Pathspecs are gitignore-style and repeatable; prefix ! to exclude. --include, --exclude, and --recursive are gone.
  • add-files runs the Prefect flow rag_file_ingestion_flow and auto-starts a Prefect server when prefect.auto_start is true. Unchanged files are skipped via a manifest unless --force is set.
  • query [TEXT] [-r NAME] [--k 4] [--filter JSON] [--full] [-l/--max-length 100].

Prefer add-files over the bundled rag_ingest workflow: at upstream commit 7fbd7a3 that workflow passes chunk_size/chunker to a flow that expects max_chunk_tokens/chunker_name and fails. The md_ingest example in workflows.md shows a working definition.

from genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.rag_flow import rag_file_ingestion_flow

rag_file_ingestion_flow(base_dir="./docs", retriever_name="docs", max_chunk_tokens=512, pathspecs=["**/*.md"])

RAG as an Agent Tool

agents:
  docs_qa:
    harness: langchain
    type: react
    llm: gpt-4o-mini@openai
    system_prompt: "Answer only from the documentation. Cite file names."
    tools:
      - factory: genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.rag_tool_factory.create_rag_tool_from_config
        config:
          retriever: hybrid
          tool_name: search_docs
          tool_description: "Search the product documentation."
          top_k: 5
from genai_tk.agents.tools.langchain.rag_tool_factory import RAGToolConfig, RAGToolFactory
from genai_tk.core.factories import get_llm

factory = RAGToolFactory(get_llm())                      # takes a BaseChatModel, not an id
tool = factory.create_tool(RAGToolConfig(retriever="hybrid", tool_name="search_docs", top_k=5))
result = await tool.ainvoke({"query": "vector search", "filter": '{"src": "a.md"}'})

RAGToolConfig fields: retriever, tool_name="rag_search", tool_description, default_filter, top_k=4. The older spec: rag_search / retriever_name: form (still shown in upstream docs/rag.md) fails validation.

Choosing a Setup

SituationSetup
Prototype or testsInMemoryBackend or Chroma ::memory:: + VectorRetriever; fake embeddings
Local persistent corpusChroma on disk + record_manager_url
Keyword-heavy content (codes, part numbers)EnsembleRetriever of vector + BM25
Precision matters more than latencyRerankedRetriever over the ensemble
Production on PostgresPgVectorBackend or PgHybridRetriever (pgvector + tsvector in one query)
Documents are PDFs/Office filesConvert first with the markdownize workflow, then ingest the Markdown

documents.label: Workflows, Prefect & Document Processing — references/workflows.md
documents.html:
Workflows, Prefect & Document Processing — references/workflows.md

genai-tk orchestrates multi-step pipelines (convert → anonymize → extract → ingest) as YAML workflows executed by Prefect. The DSL is compiled by the standalone prefect-yaml package (a core dependency); genai-tk adds the CLI, the built-in flows, ingest routing, and the markdownize converter ladder.

Workflow YAML

Workflows live under a top-level workflows: key in any YAML file picked up by :merge: (the bundled set is in config/examples/workflows.yaml).

How values reach the flow

This rule explains most workflow errors:

  • For a run: workflow, every key in defaults: and params: is passed to the callable as a keyword argument (key: ${values.key}), plus force / dry_run when set. A top-level with: on a run: workflow is ignored.
  • Before scheduling, the engine checks those names against the callable's signature and fails with unexpected argument(s) for '<target>' on any mismatch. A missing required: true param fails earlier with missing required parameter(s).
  • So defaults/params keys must be exactly the flow's parameter names.

Single-step workflow

workflows:
  md_ingest:
    description: "Chunk Markdown files into a retriever"
    run: genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.rag_flow.rag_file_ingestion_flow   # dotted callable or workflow name
    defaults:
      max_chunk_tokens: 512        # names match rag_file_ingestion_flow's signature
      chunker_name: auto
      batch_size: 10
      pathspecs: ["**/*.md"]
    params:
      base_dir: {required: true}
      retriever_name: {required: true}
    presets:
      docs:
        base_dir: "${paths.data_root}/markdown"
        retriever_name: default

Multi-step pipeline

workflows:
  anonymize_then_ingest:
    description: "Anonymize text files, then ingest them"
    pipeline:
      - id: anonymize
        run: anonymize                     # another workflow by name
        with:
          output_dir: "${values.anon_dir}"
      - id: ingest
        run: md_ingest
        after: [anonymize]                 # DAG dependency
        with:
          base_dir: "${values.anon_dir}"
    defaults:                              # sub-workflow keys resolve from THIS workflow's values
      batch_size: 10
      save_mapping: false
      faker_seed: 42
      max_chunk_tokens: 512
      chunker_name: auto
      pathspecs: ["**/*.md"]
    params:
      base_dir: {required: true}
      anon_dir: {required: true}
      retriever_name: {required: true}

When a step runs another workflow, it gets that workflow's defaults/params keys wired to ${values.*} of the parent pipeline, with the step's with: merged on top. The parent must therefore define every value its sub-workflows need.

Step keys: id, run, after (alias wait_for), with (supports ${values.*} and ${steps.<id>.result...}), cache (none | manifest | hybrid), execution, foreach, inline, artifacts.

Value precedence: CLI --set > preset > defaults.

Upstream docs/design/07_workflow_engine_and_prefect.md shows a steps: / uses: / needs: syntax; every working config uses run: / pipeline: / after: as above.

Built-in workflows

Status comes from a static check of config/examples/workflows.yaml against the flow signatures at upstream commit 7fbd7a3.

WorkflowDoesStatus
markdownize (presets docs, fast, best)Convert PDFs, Office files, images, spreadsheets, zips to MarkdownOK
merge_markdownConcatenate Markdown filesOK
anonymizePresidio + Faker PII replacement (nlp extra)OK
json_to_tableFlatten JSON results into CSV/ExcelOK
baml_runOne BAML call (see baml-structured.md)Runs, but drops output_dir/output_file
rag_ingest, anonymize_and_ingestChunk and ingest into a retrieverBroken: declares chunk_size/chunker, flow wants max_chunk_tokens/chunker_name
office2pdfOffice → PDF via LibreOfficeBroken: declares sources/pdf_output_dir, flow wants base_dir/output_dir
baml_extract, baml_to_tableBatch BAML extractionBroken: declares sources/json_output_dir, flow wants base_dir/output_dir

For ingestion, cli rag add-files calls the flow directly and works (see rag.md). For the others, define a corrected workflow in your own workflows: config (as in md_ingest above) or call the flow from Python.

CLI

uv run cli workflow list                                     # workflows and their presets
uv run cli workflow show md_ingest
uv run cli workflow validate
uv run cli workflow run md_ingest/docs --dry-run             # NAME/PRESET; show the plan
uv run cli workflow run md_ingest --set base_dir=./md --set retriever_name=docs
uv run cli workflow run markdownize/fast --set sources=./inbox --set md_output_dir=./data/md
uv run cli workflow run markdownize -p "**/*.pdf" -p "!drafts/**" --force
uv run cli workflow serve md_ingest/docs --cron "0 2 * * *"  # Prefect deployment

uv run cli prefect start        # local Prefect server (-f to force)
uv run cli prefect status
uv run cli prefect ui
uv run cli prefect stop

workflow run options: --set KEY=VALUE (repeatable), -p/--pathspec (→ values.pathspecs), --to (→ values.output_dir), --base-dir (→ values.base_dir), --force (bool), --dry-run. There is no --preset flag; select a preset with NAME/PRESET.

With prefect.auto_start: true (the default in app_conf.yaml), workflow run and rag add-files start the Prefect server themselves.

Python API

from genai_tk.workflow import execute_workflow, list_workflow_names, resolve_workflow_invocation

print(list_workflow_names())
invocation = resolve_workflow_invocation(
    "md_ingest/docs",
    cli_overrides={"retriever_name": "docs"},
)
result = execute_workflow(invocation)

Prefect flows can also be called directly, for example genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.rag_flow.rag_file_ingestion_flow(...) or genai_tk.workflow.markdownize.markdownize_flow(...). To make your own step usable from YAML, write a Prefect flow (or plain callable) in your package and reference it by dotted path in run:.

Ingest Routing

config/ingest_routes.yaml maps source items (paths or URLs) to workflows. First match wins, so put specific patterns before catch-alls.

ingest_routes:
  default:
    description: "Files → markdownize; git repos → git_repo; URLs → web_page"
    default: genai_tk.workflow.markdownize.markdownize_flow
    routes:
      - pathspec: "https://github.com/**"
        workflow: genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.git_repo_flow.git_repo_flow
      - pathspec: "**/*.git"
        workflow: genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.git_repo_flow.git_repo_flow
      - pathspec: "https://**"
        workflow: genai_tk.workflow.prefect.flows.web_page_flow.web_page_flow
      - pathspec: "**/*.pdf"
        workflow: markdownize
        with: {profile: best}

Routed workflows must accept sources: list[str] and md_output_dir: str. Unknown keys are rejected.

from genai_tk.workflow import ingest_dispatch_flow

ingest_dispatch_flow(["./inbox", "https://github.com/org/repo"], md_output_dir="./data/md", routes="default")

force_stage reruns from a given stage: unzip < pdf < md < parquet < graph < embed < all.

Markdownize (Document Conversion)

There is no dedicated markdownize CLI command; run it as a workflow:

uv run cli workflow run markdownize/best --set sources=./contracts --set md_output_dir=./data/md
uv run cli workflow run markdownize --set profile=docling --set sources=./scans --set md_output_dir=./data/md

Profiles (config/markdownize.yaml):

ProfileRouting
fastSpreadsheets → messy-XLS converter; everything else → MarkItDown
medium (default)Spreadsheets → messy-XLS; Office → PDF → Mistral OCR; PDFs → Mistral OCR; rest → MarkItDown
bestOffice and spreadsheets → PDF → Mistral OCR; PDFs → Mistral OCR; rest → MarkItDown
docling, lighton, anydoc, llmAlternative converter ladders

Existing .md files are copied, not converted. Mistral OCR needs MISTRAL_API_KEY; Docling needs the docling extra.

Converters are declared under markdownize_converters.<name>: {class, params} and created with genai_tk.extra.markdownize.factory.ConverterFactory.create(name, **overrides). A custom converter implements async convert(path) -> str.

NLP and Anonymization

nlp:
  default_language: en
  default_model: en_core_web_md

The nlp extra provides spaCy, Presidio detection, and reversible Faker replacement. The same engine powers the anonymize workflow, the AnonymizationMiddleware for agents (see agents.md), and spaCy preprocessing for BM25.

name: langchain description: > Build AI agents with LangChain v1 and LangGraph in Python. Use this skill whenever the user mentions LangChain, LangGraph, create_agent, init_chat_model, @tool, ToolRuntime, agent middleware, human-in-the-loop, structured output, MCP tools (langchain.mcp, MCPAdapter), RAG, multi-agent handoffs or subagents, checkpointers, Deep Agents (create_deep_agent) or Managed Deep Agents (mda, define_deep_agent). Also trigger for migrating from create_react_agent, LLMChain, AgentExecutor or langchain-mcp-adapters, stream_events, SummarizationMiddleware, and langchain-classic.

LangChain Skill

Build production AI agents with LangChain v1 (create_agent on top of LangGraph), its middleware system, built-in MCP support and the LangGraph runtime. Verified against langchain 1.4.6, langchain-core 1.6, langgraph 1.2 and deepagents 0.7 (Python 3.10+; deepagents needs 3.11+).

Quick Reference

TopicFile
Built-in and custom middlewarereferences/middleware.md
LangGraph graphs, persistence, durability, streamingreferences/langgraph.md
Subagents, handoffs, skills, routersreferences/multi-agent.md
Deep Agents harness and Managed Deep Agents (mda)references/deep-agents.md
RAG, embeddings, vector stores, retrieversreferences/retrieval.md

Installation

pip install -U langchain langgraph langchain-anthropic   # or langchain-openai, langchain-google-genai, ...
pip install -U "langchain[mcp]"                          # built-in MCP client (langchain.mcp, beta)
pip install -U deepagents                                # optional: planning + filesystem + subagents harness
pip install -U langchain-classic                         # only for legacy chains/retrievers

Quick Agent

from langchain.agents import create_agent

def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Get the current weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny in {city}!"

agent = create_agent(
    model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5",
    tools=[get_weather],
    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant.",
)

result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in SF?"}]})
print(result["messages"][-1].content)

create_agent returns a compiled LangGraph graph, so invoke, stream, stream_events, checkpointers, stores and interrupts all work on it. Plain functions with type hints and a docstring are accepted as tools; use @tool when you need a custom name, schema or ToolRuntime.

Model Configuration

from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model

model = init_chat_model(
    "anthropic:claude-sonnet-5",   # "provider:model"; e.g. "openai:gpt-5.5", "google_genai:gemini-3.6-flash"
    temperature=0, timeout=30, max_tokens=2000, max_retries=2,
)

model.profile["max_input_tokens"]    # model capabilities (from models.dev): context size, tool calling, modalities

Pass either the string or the model instance as model= to create_agent. system_prompt accepts a str or a SystemMessage (useful for content blocks such as provider cache-control markers).

Tools

The docstring becomes the description the model sees, and type hints become the argument schema:

from dataclasses import dataclass
from langchain.tools import tool, ToolRuntime

@tool
def search(query: str, limit: int = 10) -> str:
    """Search the order database. Returns up to `limit` matching records."""
    return f"Found {limit} results for '{query}'"

@dataclass
class Context:
    user_id: str

@tool
def get_user_data(runtime: ToolRuntime[Context]) -> str:
    """Get the current user's profile."""
    return f"Data for {runtime.context.user_id}"

ToolRuntime is injected and hidden from the model. It exposes state (messages and custom fields), context (immutable per-run data passed as agent.invoke(..., context=Context(...))), store (long-term memory), stream_writer (custom stream updates), tool_call_id and config. config and runtime are reserved argument names. Finer-grained injectables also live in langchain.tools: InjectedState, InjectedStore, InjectedToolCallId, InjectedToolArg.

Memory

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore

agent = create_agent(
    model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5",
    tools=[search],
    checkpointer=InMemorySaver(),   # short-term: per-thread conversation state
    store=InMemoryStore(),          # long-term: cross-thread memory via runtime.store
)

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "conversation-1"}}
agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi, I'm Ana"}]}, config=config)

In production use PostgresSaver/AsyncPostgresSaver or SqliteSaver (references/langgraph.md), and keep long threads in budget with SummarizationMiddleware.

Structured Output

from pydantic import BaseModel
from langchain.agents.structured_output import ToolStrategy, ProviderStrategy

class Response(BaseModel):
    answer: str
    confidence: float | None = None

agent = create_agent(model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5", tools=[search],
                     response_format=ToolStrategy(Response))
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]})   # result["structured_response"]: Response
response_formatBehavior
Response (bare type)Auto: provider-native JSON schema when the model profile supports it, else tool calling
ToolStrategy(Response, handle_errors=True)Structured output via an artificial tool call; retries on validation errors; works with any tool-calling model
ProviderStrategy(Response, strict=True)Provider-native structured output (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, ...)

Schemas can be Pydantic models, dataclasses, TypedDicts or JSON schema dicts. Outside agents, use model.with_structured_output(Response).

Middleware

Middleware is the v1 extension point that replaces pre/post hooks. Built-ins live in langchain.agents.middleware:

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import (
    SummarizationMiddleware, HumanInTheLoopMiddleware, ModelFallbackMiddleware,
    ToolCallLimitMiddleware, PIIMiddleware,
)
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

agent = create_agent(
    model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5",
    tools=[search, send_email],
    checkpointer=InMemorySaver(),   # required for interrupts
    middleware=[
        SummarizationMiddleware(model="openai:gpt-5.4-mini", trigger=("fraction", 0.8), keep=("messages", 20)),
        ModelFallbackMiddleware("openai:gpt-5.5"),
        ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="search", run_limit=5),
        PIIMiddleware("email", strategy="redact", apply_to_input=True),
        HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={"send_email": {"allowed_decisions": ["approve", "edit", "reject"]}}),
    ],
)

Custom middleware uses decorators (before_agent, before_model, after_model, after_agent, wrap_model_call, wrap_tool_call, dynamic_prompt) or an AgentMiddleware subclass:

from langchain.agents.middleware import dynamic_prompt, wrap_tool_call, ModelRequest

@dynamic_prompt
def tiered_prompt(request: ModelRequest) -> str:
    return f"You are a support agent. Customer tier: {request.runtime.context.tier}."

@wrap_tool_call
def audit_tool_calls(request, handler):
    print("calling", request.tool_call["name"], request.tool_call["args"])
    return handler(request)

Full catalogue (retries, tool selection, context editing, to-do lists, shell, emulators) and patterns (dynamic models, dynamic tools, jumps) are in references/middleware.md.

Human-in-the-Loop

With HumanInTheLoopMiddleware and a checkpointer, the run pauses before the listed tools. Resume with one decision per pending action:

from langgraph.types import Command

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "t1"}}
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Email Bob the report"}]},
                      config=config, version="v2")
while result.interrupts:
    actions = result.interrupts[0].value["action_requests"]
    for action in actions:
        print("Pending:", action["name"], action["args"])
    decisions = [{"type": "approve"} for _ in actions]   # one decision per action, in order
    result = agent.invoke(Command(resume={"decisions": decisions}), config=config, version="v2")

Decision types: {"type": "approve"}, {"type": "edit", "edited_action": {"name": ..., "args": {...}}}, {"type": "reject", "message": "why"}, and {"type": "respond", "message": "..."}. With version="v2", invoke returns a GraphOutput (.value, .interrupts) instead of a plain dict.

Streaming

Use event streaming (version="v3") for apps and UIs. It returns a run object with typed projections:

stream = agent.stream_events({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in SF?"}]}, version="v3")
for kind, item in stream.interleave("messages", "tool_calls"):
    if kind == "messages":
        for token in item.text:
            print(token, end="", flush=True)
    else:
        print(f"\n[tool] {item.tool_name}({item.input})")
        for delta in item.output_deltas:   # drain first: item.output is None until the tool finishes
            print(delta, end="", flush=True)
        print(f"\n[result] {item.output}")
final_state = stream.output

Event streaming is experimental in LangGraph 1.2 (it emits a LangChainBetaWarning). Classic agent.stream(input, stream_mode=["updates", "messages", "custom"]) still works; the model node is "model".

MCP Integration

LangChain 1.4 ships a built-in MCP client, langchain.mcp (beta, built on FastMCP). It replaces langchain-mcp-adapters' MultiServerMCPClient:

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.mcp import MCPAdapter

config = {"mcpServers": {
    "math": {"command": "python", "args": ["/path/to/math_server.py"]},             # stdio
    "api": {"url": "https://api.example.com/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer TOKEN"}},
}}

async def build_agent():
    async with MCPAdapter(config) as adapter:     # or MCPAdapter("https://..."), MCPAdapter(Path("server.py"))
        tools = await adapter.list_tools()        # multi-server tools are prefixed: math_..., api_...
    return create_agent("anthropic:claude-sonnet-5", tools)
  • A plain string target must be an http(s) URL; reach local servers with pathlib.Path(...) or a config.
  • Tools stay usable after the async with block exits. They are async, so run the agent with ainvoke/astream.
  • Server elicitation requests become LangGraph interrupt()s, so add a checkpointer.
  • Interceptors are gone: use @wrap_tool_call middleware (MCP provenance is in request.tool.metadata["mcp"]).

State Updates from Tools

Return a Command to update state or control flow:

from langchain.messages import RemoveMessage, ToolMessage
from langchain.tools import tool, ToolRuntime
from langgraph.graph.message import REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES
from langgraph.types import Command

@tool
def clear_history() -> Command:
    """Clear the conversation history."""
    return Command(update={"messages": [RemoveMessage(id=REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES)]})

@tool
def set_language(language: str, runtime: ToolRuntime) -> Command:
    """Remember the user's preferred language."""
    return Command(update={
        "language": language,   # custom field: needs state_schema= (a TypedDict extending AgentState)
        "messages": [ToolMessage(f"Language set to {language}", tool_call_id=runtime.tool_call_id)],
    })

Deep Agents

deepagents wraps create_agent with a virtual filesystem, a task tool for subagents, summarization, and optional skills, memory files, permissions and sandboxes, for long multi-step tasks. Managed Deep Agents (managed-deepagents, CLI mda) deploys the same harness to LangSmith from a project directory (agent.py with define_deep_agent, instructions.md, memory.py, sandbox/, schedules/). Both are covered in references/deep-agents.md.

from deepagents import create_deep_agent

agent = create_deep_agent(
    model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5",
    tools=[internet_search],
    system_prompt="You are an expert researcher. Write the final report to /report.md.",
    subagents=[{"name": "critic", "description": "Reviews drafts", "system_prompt": "You are a strict reviewer."}],
)

Full Production Agent

from dataclasses import dataclass
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import SummarizationMiddleware, ToolRetryMiddleware
from langchain.agents.structured_output import ToolStrategy
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langchain.tools import tool, ToolRuntime
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

@dataclass
class Context:
    user_id: str

@tool
def search_orders(query: str, runtime: ToolRuntime[Context]) -> str:
    """Search the current user's orders by keyword, date or status."""
    return f"Orders for {runtime.context.user_id}: {query}"

@dataclass
class Response:
    answer: str
    order_ids: list[str] | None = None

agent = create_agent(
    model=init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-sonnet-5", temperature=0),
    system_prompt="You are a customer service agent.",
    tools=[search_orders],
    context_schema=Context,
    response_format=ToolStrategy(Response),
    middleware=[ToolRetryMiddleware(max_retries=2), SummarizationMiddleware("openai:gpt-5.4-mini", trigger=("tokens", 4000))],
    checkpointer=InMemorySaver(),
)

result = agent.invoke(
    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Find my recent orders"}]},
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "session-1"}},
    context=Context(user_id="user123"),
)
print(result["structured_response"])

Migrating to v1

Old (0.x / pre-1.4)Current
langgraph.prebuilt.create_react_agentlangchain.agents.create_agent
prompt=system_prompt= (static) or @dynamic_prompt middleware
pre_model_hook / post_model_hook@before_model / @after_model middleware
config["configurable"] for user datacontext_schema= + invoke(..., context=...)
AgentExecutor, LLMChain, RetrievalQA, langchain.retrieverscreate_agent, or langchain_classic.* for legacy code
langchain.text_splitterlangchain_text_splitters
langchain_mcp_adapters.client.MultiServerMCPClientlangchain.mcp.MCPAdapter
MCP tool_interceptors@wrap_tool_call middleware
Prompted structured outputToolStrategy / ProviderStrategy
message.content parsing for reasoning/citationsmessage.content_blocks (standard blocks)

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

  • Tools without type hints or docstrings: the docstring is the tool description the model sees; a missing or vague one means the agent misuses the tool
  • Global state in tools: read per-user data from ToolRuntime[Context], not globals, so tools stay testable and safe in concurrent runs
  • No checkpointer, then wondering why the agent forgets: multi-turn agents, human-in-the-loop and MCP elicitation all need a checkpointer plus a stable thread_id
  • Hand-rolled hook loops: use middleware (SummarizationMiddleware, ModelFallbackMiddleware, ToolRetryMiddleware, limits) instead of wrapping agent.invoke in custom retry/trim code
  • Letting raw tool exceptions reach the model or user: use ToolErrorMiddleware(on_error=...) or ToolRetryMiddleware, and return the exception type rather than internal details
  • Importing removed modules: langchain.vectorstores, langchain.document_loaders, langchain.text_splitter, langchain.retrievers and LLMChain no longer exist in langchain v1; use provider packages, langchain_core, langchain_text_splitters or langchain_classic
  • Starting new code on langchain-mcp-adapters or create_react_agent: both are superseded by langchain.mcp and create_agent
  • Passing a local script path as a string to MCPAdapter: strings must be URLs; use Path(...) or an mcpServers config for stdio servers
  • Stuffing whole documents into context: use the retrieval patterns in references/retrieval.md

When to Use / Not Use

Use this skill when:

  • Building agents with LangChain v1 or LangGraph in Python
  • Adding tools, memory, middleware, human approval, MCP servers or structured output to an LLM app
  • Implementing RAG, subagents, handoffs, routers, Deep Agents (self-hosted or managed) or stateful workflows
  • Migrating 0.x code (create_react_agent, AgentExecutor, chains, langchain-mcp-adapters)

Do NOT use this skill when:

  • A single stateless LLM call is all you need; the plain provider SDK is lighter
  • The project standardizes on another agent framework; follow the project's stack
  • The agent is code-first and benefits from the smaller SmolAgents execution model; see the smolagents skill

Key Links

  • Docs: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/overview
  • Middleware: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/built-in
  • MCP: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/mcp/connections
  • From langchain-mcp-adapters: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/migrate/langchain-mcp-adapters
  • Event streaming: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/event-streaming
  • Deep Agents: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview
  • Managed Deep Agents: https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-overview
  • API reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python
