documents.label: SKILL.md
documents.html:
name: prime-rl description: > Post-train LLMs with PrimeIntellect's prime-rl (async RL, SFT, distillation, evals). Use this skill whenever the user mentions prime-rl, wants to write an rl.toml or sft.toml, run uv run rl / uv run sft / uv run eval / uv run inference, pick GRPO, MaxRL, OPD or ECHO, tune IPO loss, or monitor and resume a run. Also trigger for verifiers environments, Prime Intellect post-training, reverse-text, and pydantic-config TOML overrides.

prime-rl Post-Training

prime-rl is Prime Intellect's framework for asynchronous RL and SFT post-training at scale. One launch (uv run rl) starts a vLLM inference server, a CPU-only orchestrator that collects rollouts from verifiers environments, and an FSDP trainer that pushes new weights back to inference. This skill teaches how to install it, write configs, choose an algorithm, launch and monitor runs, evaluate checkpoints, and export weights.

Facts are checked against upstream commit dd72f0f (2026-10-13, v0.9.0). When the docs and the code disagree, this skill follows the code (see Doc Drift).

Quick Reference

TopicReferenceWhen to read
Install, uv sync, extras, env packagesreferences/install.mdFresh machine, missing env package, DeepEP/kernels
Config system (TOML + CLI)references/configs.mdWriting or overriding any config, config errors
Algorithms, losses, advantages, curricula, renderersreferences/algorithms.mdChoosing GRPO vs OPD vs SFT-distill, tuning the loss
rl / sft / inference, run dirs, checkpoints, resume, exportreferences/training-runs.mdLaunching, resuming, exporting to HF
Logs, metrics, dashboard, check-in runbookreferences/monitoring.mdChecking on or debugging a live run
uv run eval, task selectionreferences/eval.mdBenchmarking a model or checkpoint
Multi-GPU, multi-node, SLURM, LoRA, MoE, inference servingreferences/scaling.mdAnything beyond one node with defaults

Core Workflow

  1. Install on a Linux box with NVIDIA GPUs (the smoke run needs 2):
   curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
   cd prime-rl && uv sync --all-extras
  1. Smoke-test with the bundled example before touching anything else:
   uv run rl @ examples/basic/reverse-text/rl.toml
  1. Write your config (TOML, snake_case) by copying the closest example under examples/.
  2. Dry-run to resolve and validate it without launching:
   uv run rl @ my-rl.toml --dry-run --run.name check
  1. Launch with a predictable run name and checkpoints so the run can be resumed:
   uv run rl @ my-rl.toml --run.name my-run --ckpt.interval 25 --ckpt.keep-last 3
  1. Monitor logs, metrics and the dashboard (see Monitoring).
  2. Evaluate with uv run eval against a uv run inference server.
  3. Export the DCP checkpoint to HF safetensors with tools/convert_dcp_to_bf16.py.

Entrypoints

Always run through uv run; never call python, torchrun or vllm serve directly.

CommandPurposeNotes
uv run rlFull RL pipeline: inference + orchestrator + trainerRLConfig; local or SLURM ([slurm])
uv run sftDataset-based SFTLaunches torchrun itself; optional online evals
uv run inferencevLLM server with prime-rl endpointsRouter on port 8000, engine on 8100; adds /update_weights, /load_lora_adapter, /init_broadcaster
uv run evalStandalone multi-env evalOne epoch per source; --resume continues
uv run orchestrator / trainer / env-serverPieces of rl for manual layoutsRarely needed
uv run dashboardLocal web dashboard (port 7788)Read-only on run dirs

Config Essentials

Every entrypoint takes TOML files with @ plus dotted CLI overrides (pydantic-config).

uv run rl @ base.toml @ overlay.toml --max-steps 50 --orchestrator.train.group-size 16
uv run rl --help                         # every field with its default
  • Precedence: CLI > files (left to right, deep merge) > class defaults.
  • CLI is kebab-case (--trainer.optim.lr), TOML is snake_case (lr).
  • Booleans: --flag / --no-flag on the CLI, explicit true/false in TOML.
  • None is the string "None" in TOML.
  • No inline tables (key = { ... }). Use [section] headers or dotted keys.
  • Lists are replaced wholesale by later files; repeat the full list in overlays.
  • Optional sections ([ckpt], [inference], [monitors.wandb]) are enabled by an empty header.
  • Unions pick a variant with type ([trainer.loss] type = "icepop").
  • Renamed fields fail as unknown keys on purpose. Fix the config; do not expect aliases.

Minimal RL Config

This is the upstream reverse-text example (examples/basic/reverse-text/rl.toml), trimmed of W&B:

max_steps = 20
seq_len = 2048

[model]
name = "PrimeIntellect/Qwen3-0.6B-Reverse-Text-SFT"

[orchestrator]
batch_size = 128

[orchestrator.train]
group_size = 16

[orchestrator.train.sampling]
max_completion_tokens = 128

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
name = "reverse-text"
env.taskset.id = "reverse-text"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

[orchestrator.eval]
interval = 5

[[orchestrator.eval.source]]
name = "reverse-text-eval"
select.limit = 256
env.taskset.id = "reverse-text"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

[trainer.optim]
lr = 3e-6

[ckpt]

[inference]

[orchestrator.renderer]
name = "prime-qwen3"

Key points:

  • [[orchestrator.train.source]] is one block per environment. Nested env settings are dotted keys inside that block, not separate [...source.env] headers.
  • orchestrator.train.group_size defaults to 1. With GRPO that makes every advantage zero and the trainer learns nothing. Set it to 8 or more.
  • [inference] (even empty) tells rl to launch the policy server. Leave it out only when you start the inference server yourself.
  • [orchestrator.renderer] name = "auto" is the default. Fine-tunes whose name does not match the renderer map need an explicit renderer (here prime-qwen3).

Choosing an Algorithm

Set [orchestrator.train.algo] type. Each type's class defaults are its vetted setting.

typeSignalNeedsUse for
grpo (default)RL on actions, group-mean baselinegroup_size ≥ 8Standard verifiable-reward RL
max_rlRL, mean-normalized group creditgroup_size ≥ 8Upweighting hard tasks
raeRL, per-agent EMA baselineMulti-agent envSelf-play (for example kuhn-poker)
hierarchical_grpoRL, per-role baselinesProposer-solver env, episode_agentsProposer-solver training
opdReverse KL to a teacher[orchestrator.train.algo.teacher] on vLLMOn-policy distillation
sftCE on a frozen model's samples[orchestrator.train.algo.sampling.source]Hard distillation on the fly
opsdReverse KL to demo-conditioned selfdemo_key in task infoSelf-distillation
echoGRPO + weighted CE on env tokensRenderer role attributionLearning from tool output
[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "opd"

[orchestrator.train.algo.teacher]
name = "Qwen/Qwen3-32B"
base_url = "http://localhost:8001/v1"

prime-rl only hosts the policy. Start frozen teachers yourself, for example CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-32B --server.port 8001.

The RL loss lives in [trainer.loss]. Omit it to get IPO (eps = 0.3, adv_tau = 1.0). Other types are icepop, ppo, cispo and custom. Details: references/algorithms.md.

SFT

max_steps = 100

[model]
name = "PrimeIntellect/Qwen3-0.6B"

[data]
name = "willcb/R1-reverse-wikipedia-paragraphs-v1-1000"
seq_len = 4096
batch_size = 32

[optim]
lr = 2e-5

[ckpt]
uv run sft @ examples/basic/reverse-text/sft.toml --monitors.wandb

Datasets use prompt/completion columns or a messages column (messages wins if both exist). Tokenization always goes through a renderer ([renderer] name = "auto" by default). In SFT the optimizer is top-level [optim]; in RL it is [trainer.optim]. Online evals, column mapping and loss masks: references/training-runs.md.

Run Directories, Checkpoints and Resume

Each launch writes to <output_dir>/<run_name> (output_dir defaults to $PRL_OUTPUT_DIR, else outputs). Without --run.name the name is auto-generated as <envs>--<model>--<short-id>.

uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 10 --ckpt --run.name my-run              # first leg
uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 20 --ckpt --resume --run.name my-run     # continue to step 20
uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 20 --ckpt --resume.step 10 --run.name my-run
uv run python tools/convert_dcp_to_bf16.py outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_20
uv run inference --vllm.model outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_20/weights
  • Checkpoints are off by default. --ckpt saves at the end; --ckpt.interval N adds periodic saves; --ckpt.keep-last K and --ckpt.keep-interval M control retention.
  • --max-steps on resume is the final target step, not the remaining delta.
  • Reusing a run name fails unless you pass --resume or --clean (which wipes that run dir).
  • Export rejects LoRA checkpoints.

Monitoring Essentials

tail -F outputs/my-run/logs/latest/{trainer,orchestrator,inference}.log
grep -E "WARNING|ERROR" outputs/my-run/logs/latest/envs/{train,eval}/*.log
cat ~/.cache/prime-rl/dashboard/daemon.json      # live dashboard URL (default port 7788)
WatchMetricHealthy sign
Progresstrain/agg/effective/<agent>/reward/meanTrends up over hundreds of steps
Truncationtrain/agg/effective/<agent>/is_truncated/meanLow; raise max_completion_tokens if high
Off-policy driftmismatch_kl/all/meanFlat; a growing mean warns of collapse
Collapseentropy/all/meanNot collapsing toward zero
Divergenceoptim/grad_normNo spikes
Bottlenecktrainer time/wait_for_batch vs orchestrator time/wait_for_policyHigh wait_for_batch means add inference; high wait_for_policy means add trainer GPUs

When an agent monitors a run for a researcher: append check-ins to <run_dir>/STATUS.md, and never kill, restart or launch runs yourself. Hand the researcher the exact command. Full runbook: references/monitoring.md.

Eval

uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B                               # terminal 1
uv run eval reverse-text -n 32 -r 4 -m Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --client.base_url http://localhost:8000/v1                                 # terminal 2
uv run eval @ examples/basic/reverse-text/eval.toml --run.name rt-eval --resume

-n caps tasks, -r sets rollouts per task, -c pins concurrency, -s shuffles. Always cap smoke evals. Multi-source TOML and selection rules: references/eval.md.

Rules of Thumb

  • Start from examples/basic/reverse-text/ on 2 GPUs. If it finishes, your install is good.
  • orchestrator.batch_size ≥ 64 (128–512 for ablations); group_size ≥ 8 (16–32 is common).
  • Use --dry-run before every SLURM submit; validators fail fast there and slowly in the queue.
  • orchestrator.max_off_policy_steps (default 8) is the main async dial: raise it for throughput, lower it for on-policyness, and watch mismatch_kl while tuning.
  • Keep trainer.model.optimization_dtype and reduce_dtype at their defaults unless asked.

Doc Drift

Upstream docs and skills disagree with the code in a few places at dd72f0f. Trust the code.

TopicUpstream textCode / this skill
IPO eps defaultskills/configs says 0.1IPOLossConfig.eps = 0.3 (docs/algorithms.md agrees)
Loss typesDocs list ipo, icepop, customAlso ppo (clip 0.8–1.2) and cispo (ratio_high 5.0)
Renamed fieldsskills/training/start-run says validation aliases keep old keys workingPolicy is no aliases; old keys fail as unknown
Metric namesdocs/training.md uses reward/{all,env}/meanCurrent keys are train/{agg,<env>}/{all,effective}/<agent>/reward/mean
LoRA + NCCLdocs/advanced.md says NCCL falls back to filesystemOnly when [weight_broadcast] is unset; explicit nccl/nixl with LoRA raises
Throughput recipedocs/scaling.md uses [model], [model.compile]Those are SFT paths; RL uses [trainer.model]
Fused LM headdocs/scaling.md says SFT disables itfused_lm_head_token_chunk_size applies to SFT too

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

  • Leaving group_size at its default of 1 with GRPO — every advantage is zero and batches are skipped.
  • Calling vllm serve, torchrun or raw python — use uv run inference, uv run sft, uv run.
  • Inline TOML tables (env = { taskset = { id = "x" } }) — use dotted keys in the source block.
  • Partial list overlays — a later file replaces the whole [[...source]] list.
  • CLI list indexes (--orchestrator.eval.source.0.env.taskset.id) — not parsed; edit TOML or pass JSON.
  • Launching without --run.name when you will need to resume — auto names are hard to find.
  • Passing remaining steps on resume — --max-steps is the absolute target.
  • Pointing opd at "policy" or a non-vLLM teacher — rejected (zero KL) or missing prompt_logprobs.
  • uv sync without --all-packages after installing env packages — it removes them.
  • Agents restarting or killing runs on their own — hand the command to the researcher.
  • Trusting a mean reward without reading traces — check a few episodes in the dashboard.

When to Use / Not Use

Use this skill when:

  • Writing or debugging rl.toml, sft.toml or eval.toml for prime-rl.
  • Choosing between GRPO, MaxRL, OPD, SFT-distill, OPSD, ECHO, RAE or hierarchical GRPO.
  • Launching, resuming, monitoring or exporting a prime-rl run, locally or on SLURM.
  • Evaluating a model or checkpoint on verifiers environments with uv run eval.

Do not use this skill when:

  • Fine-tuning with Unsloth or Hugging Face Jobs (use unsloth-hf-jobs).
  • Writing a verifiers environment itself (taskset, harness, rubric); see the verifiers repo.
  • Serving models in production without training (use plain vLLM docs).
  • Contributing kernels or cutting prime-rl releases (see upstream skills/kernels and skills/release).

documents.label: Algorithms, Losses, Advantages, Curricula and Renderers
documents.html:
Algorithms, Losses, Advantages, Curricula and Renderers

prime-rl splits post-training into two independent choices:

  • The algorithm ([orchestrator.train.algo], on the orchestrator) decides who samples rollouts and what per-token signal each token gets (advantage, CE target or reference logprobs).
  • The RL loss ([trainer.loss], on the trainer) decides how the rl component turns advantages into gradients. The trainer is algorithm-blind.

The total loss is a sum of three components, each normalized by its own token count: rl (the configured RL loss), ce (masked NLL) and ref_kl (reverse KL to a reference model).

Algorithms

type names the algorithm, and its class defaults are the vetted setting. Any key you add beyond type is your own variant.

typeSamplingLoss componentKey fields
grpo (default)policyrllength_penalty, length_weighted_baseline = false, loss_aggregation = "token"
max_rlpolicyrlnone (mean-normalized group credit, upweights hard tasks ~1/p)
raepolicyrldecay = 0.95 (per-agent EMA baseline; group_size = 1 is fine)
hierarchical_grpopolicyrlepisode_agents (required, for example ["solver"])
opdpolicyref_klteacher (name, base_url; must be a vLLM server)
sftfrozen teachercesampling.source (name, base_url; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
opsdpolicyref_kldemo_key = "demonstration", template, renderer
echopolicyrl + ce on env tokensroles.<role>.alpha (default tool at 0.1), optional filter

GRPO and variants

The default advantage is group reward minus group mean (DR-GRPO without std normalization). A group where every rollout scores the same gets zero advantage and contributes nothing, which is why group_size must be well above 1 (8 minimum, 16–32 common).

[orchestrator.train]
group_size = 16

[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "grpo"
length_weighted_baseline = true
loss_aggregation = "prompt"   # MiMo-style prompt-mean; every rl env in the run must match

[orchestrator.train.algo.length_penalty]
type = "linear"               # output 0.25, input 0.1, turns 0.1 weights by default

Distillation

prime-rl only hosts the trainable policy. Start teachers yourself and point base_url at them:

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-32B --server.port 8001
# On-policy distillation: policy samples, reverse KL to the teacher
[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "opd"

[orchestrator.train.algo.teacher]
name = "Qwen/Qwen3-32B"
base_url = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
# Hard distillation: teacher samples, policy trains with CE on its tokens
[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "sft"

[orchestrator.train.algo.sampling.source]
name = "Qwen/Qwen3-32B"
base_url = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
# Self-distillation conditioned on a demonstration from task info
[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "opsd"
demo_key = "demonstration"

Validation rules: frozen-model sampling can only feed ce; opd cannot use "policy" as teacher (zero KL); sft without a frozen source is rejected. Use the standalone uv run sft entrypoint for plain dataset SFT; the sft algorithm is for teacher-generated supervision on the fly.

ECHO

GRPO on actions plus weighted CE on env-provided tokens selected by message role. Setting any role replaces the whole role table.

[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "echo"

[orchestrator.train.algo.roles.tool]
alpha = 0.25

[orchestrator.train.algo.roles.user]
alpha = 0.05

[orchestrator.train.algo.filter]
import_path = "my_module.drop_warnings"

[orchestrator.train.algo.filter.kwargs]
patterns = ["WARNING"]

Self-play and proposer-solver

[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "rae"
decay = 0.95

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
name = "kuhn-poker"
env.taskset.id = "kuhn-poker"
env.player0.harness.id = "null"
env.player0.runtime.type = "subprocess"
env.player1.harness.id = "null"
env.player1.runtime.type = "subprocess"
[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "hierarchical_grpo"
episode_agents = ["solver"]

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
name = "proposer-solver"
group_size = 4   # proposed problems per source task
env.n = 4        # solver attempts per proposed problem
env.taskset.id = "proposer-solver"
env.proposer.harness.id = "null"
env.proposer.runtime.type = "subprocess"
env.solver.harness.id = "null"
env.solver.runtime.type = "subprocess"

Per-env algorithms

Each train source inherits the group algorithm. A source that sets a different algo.type runs its own algorithm; one that sets only params keeps the group's type with those params changed.

[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "grpo"

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
name = "math"
env.taskset.id = "math"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
name = "terminal"
algo.type = "echo"
env.taskset.id = "terminal"
env.agent.harness.id = "bash"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

New algorithms

There is no config hook for user code. A new algorithm is a class in the repo: subclass prime_rl.orchestrator.train.algo.base.Algorithm, implement score_group (group-relative) or score_episode (per-rollout or model calls), add a config class to prime_rl.configs.algorithm, and register it in ALGORITHM_CLASSES.

RL Losses ([trainer.loss])

typeDefaultsMechanism
ipo (default)eps = 0.3, max_importance_ratio = 1e4, adv_tau = 1.0Masks tokens whose absolute probability change exceeds eps
icepopratio_low = 0.2, ratio_high = 5.0, adv_tau = 1.0Masks tokens whose importance ratio leaves the band
pporatio_low = 0.8, ratio_high = 1.2, max_importance_ratio = 1e4Clipped surrogate
cisporatio_low = 0.0, ratio_high = 5.0Clipped detached importance weight
customimport_path, kwargsYour per-sequence loss function

Omit [trainer.loss] for IPO defaults. The ce and ref_kl components are not affected.

Why eps = 0.3: in upstream's GLM-4.5-Air SWE ablation (docs/ipo.md), 0.3 masked about 0.25% of tokens; the older 0.1 masked about 2% and collapsed entropy; IcePop's mismatch KL blew up near step 1.2k. Reproduce with examples/advanced/glm-4.5-air/ipo-ablation/{base,ipo,icepop}.toml.

Custom loss

# my_module.py
import torch
from prime_rl.trainer.rl.loss import LossInputs, LossOutputs


def ppo_clip_loss(inputs: LossInputs, clip_eps: float = 0.2) -> LossOutputs:
    ratio = torch.exp(inputs.trainer_logprobs - inputs.inference_logprobs)
    clipped = torch.clamp(ratio, 1 - clip_eps, 1 + clip_eps)
    loss = -torch.min(ratio * inputs.advantages, clipped * inputs.advantages)[inputs.loss_mask].sum()
    return LossOutputs(loss=loss, metrics={"clip_frac": (ratio != clipped)[inputs.loss_mask].float().mean()})
[trainer.loss]
type = "custom"
import_path = "my_module.ppo_clip_loss"

[trainer.loss.kwargs]
clip_eps = 0.2

LossInputs carries trainer_logprobs, inference_logprobs, ref_logprobs, advantages, loss_mask and loss_weights for one sequence. Values in metrics are averaged and logged.

Async and Off-Policy

Training is asynchronous by default: while the trainer produces policy n, inference samples step n+1 rollouts with policy n-1. orchestrator.max_off_policy_steps (default 8) bounds how stale a trained rollout may be; older episodes are dropped. Raise it for throughput on long agentic rollouts, lower it for tighter on-policy training, and watch off_policy/* and mismatch_kl. There is no max_async_level field.

orchestrator.constant_trainer_batch_size = true (default) refills batches after filtering zero-signal samples so the trainer always sees orchestrator.batch_size traces. Set it to false for faster collection with smaller batches.

Curricula

Each train source has a curriculum: one task sampler plus optional admission gates. Sampler and gate state is checkpointed and logged under curriculum/<env>/.

[orchestrator.train.source.curriculum.sampler]
type = "difficulty_pool"

[orchestrator.train.source.curriculum.sampler.pools.hard]
threshold = 0.25
weight = 0.2

[orchestrator.train.source.curriculum.sampler.pools.normal]
threshold = 0.75
weight = 1.0

[orchestrator.train.source.curriculum.sampler.pools.easy]
threshold = 1.0
weight = 0.2

[orchestrator.train.source.curriculum.gates.low_signal]
type = "advantage_range"
reject_min = -0.05
reject_max = 0.05

These sections attach to the most recent [[orchestrator.train.source]] block, so place them right after the source they configure.

Multi-Turn Trajectories and Renderers

Each LLM call in a multi-turn rollout is a trajectory step. Steps merge into one training sample while each prompt is an exact token prefix of the next (the extension property). When it breaks, the trainer starts a new sample instead of training on corrupted tokens.

Renderers keep the prefix exact by extending prior tokens instead of re-rendering the chat template (Qwen3's template, for example, strips past <think> blocks). Hand-coded renderers ship for qwen3, qwen3-vl, qwen3.5, glm-5, glm-4.5, minimax-m2, deepseek-v3, kimi-k2, kimi-k2.5, nemotron-3 and gpt-oss; everything else falls back to DefaultRenderer.

[orchestrator.renderer]
name = "auto"          # detect from the tokenizer

# Fine-tunes whose name misses the renderer map need an explicit name
# name = "prime-qwen3"

# Out-of-tree renderer
# name = "custom"
# import_path = "my_renderers.MyRenderer"

SFT uses the same renderer config at top-level [renderer].

documents.label: prime-rl Config System
documents.html:
prime-rl Config System

Every prime-rl entrypoint is configured with pydantic-config: typed Pydantic classes loaded from TOML (or YAML/JSON) files plus CLI overrides. Config classes live in packages/prime-rl-configs/src/prime_rl/configs/ (rl.py, sft.py, eval.py, inference.py, orchestrator.py, trainer.py, algorithm.py).

Loading and Composition

uv run rl @ examples/basic/reverse-text/rl.toml                     # one file
uv run rl @ examples/basic/reverse-text/rl.toml --max-steps 50      # CLI override
uv run rl @ base.toml @ overlay.toml                                # merge left to right
uv run rl @ base.toml --trainer @ trainer.toml --trainer.optim.lr 1e-6   # section file + override
uv run rl --help                                                    # every field and default
  • Precedence: CLI > config files (left to right) > class defaults.
  • Merging is deep: fields an overlay leaves unset keep the base value.
  • output_dir adds one fallback: CLI > files > $PRL_OUTPUT_DIR > "outputs".
  • CLI uses kebab-case (--inference.vllm.max-model-len); TOML uses snake_case (max_model_len).

Inspect and Validate

uv run rl @ rl.toml --dry-run --output-dir /tmp/x --run.name check
ls /tmp/x/check/configs/latest/resolved/      # rl.json, trainer.json, orchestrator.json, ...
cat /tmp/x/check/configs/latest/command.txt   # shell-safe launch command

Every launch writes configs/attempt_<n>/ with command.txt, the launch TOML and resolved/. configs/latest points to the current attempt. Validators for incompatible combinations (for example context parallelism without flash attention) run at resolve time, so --dry-run catches them.

TOML Rules

No inline tables

# Wrong
[[orchestrator.train.source]]
env = { taskset = { id = "reverse-text" } }

# Right
[[orchestrator.train.source]]
env.taskset.id = "reverse-text"

Sources are one block

Inside a [[...source]] entry, nested sub-configs are dotted keys in the same block. Nested arrays of tables (for example judges) keep full-path headers and attach to the preceding source.

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
name = "reverse-text"
ratio = 1.0
env.taskset.id = "reverse-text"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

[[orchestrator.eval.source]]
name = "reverse-text-eval"
env.taskset.id = "reverse-text"
env.taskset.split = "test"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

ratio weights multiple train sources (default 1.0).

Group defaults

Source groups hold defaults that every source inherits: [orchestrator.train], [orchestrator.eval], the SFT [eval] block, and the top level of an eval TOML. Shared fields are env, sampling, select, group_size, plus algo on train and interval on online eval. Blocks merge key by key and a source's own value wins. A source block with a different type (for example algo.type = "echo") replaces the group's block for that source.

Scalars

KindTOMLCLI
Booleanenable_prefix_caching = true--flag / --no-flag
Nonemax_model_len = "None"--inference.vllm.max-model-len None
Listarray of tables, replaced wholesalespace-separated or JSON
Dicta [section]JSON string: --trainer.env-vars '{"KEY": "v"}'

JSON on the CLI only works for plain dict fields. Nested model fields (like algo) need dotted keys (--orchestrator.train.algo.type max_rl) or a TOML overlay.

Lists on the CLI

There are no list-index paths: --orchestrator.eval.source.0.env.taskset.id does not parse. Either edit TOML or replace the whole list with JSON:

uv run rl @ rl.toml --orchestrator.eval.source '[{"env": {"taskset": {"id": "reverse-text"}}}]'

Optional sections

Fields typed SomeConfig | None are off until set. A bare flag or an empty header enables defaults; a nested key enables and sets:

--ckpt                      # checkpoint at the end of training
--ckpt.interval 25          # enables and sets the interval
--monitors.wandb            # enable W&B with defaults
--no-monitors.wandb         # disable
--monitors.wandb.project rt # enables W&B and sets the project
[ckpt]        # same as --ckpt
[inference]   # rl launches the policy server

Discriminated unions

Set type to choose a variant; omit it to keep the default.

[orchestrator.train.algo]
type = "max_rl"

[trainer.loss]
type = "icepop"

[trainer.optim]
type = "muon"

[trainer.scheduler]
type = "cosine"
warmup_steps = 10
UnionVariants (default first)
orchestrator.train.algogrpo, max_rl, rae, hierarchical_grpo, opd, opsd, sft, echo
trainer.lossipo, icepop, ppo, cispo, custom
trainer.optimadamw, muon, sign_sgd
trainer.schedulerconstant, linear, cosine
deploymentsingle_node, multi_node

vLLM pass-through

[inference.vllm] uses vLLM's own argument names and forwards any key to the server:

[inference.vllm]
model = "Qwen/Qwen3-4B"
tensor_parallel_size = 2
max_model_len = 16384
max_num_seqs = 256
--inference.vllm.max-num-seqs 256
--inference.vllm.compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}'

Non-vLLM knobs (router, deployment, weight broadcast, KV-cache offload, env vars) stay on [inference] itself.

Shared Top-Level Keys (rl)

RLConfig propagates some keys to the trainer and orchestrator so you set them once:

KeyEffect
max_steps, seq_lenTraining length and sequence length
[model] namePolicy model for trainer, orchestrator and inference
[ckpt]Checkpointing (interval, keep_last, keep_interval)
[monitors.wandb], [monitors.prime], [monitors.file]Logging targets (file is on by default)
[log] levelLog level for trainer and orchestrator
[deployment], [slurm]GPU layout and cluster submission
output_dir, [run] name, clean, [resume]Run directory management
env_varsExtra environment variables for every component
dashboardAuto-start the dashboard daemon (default true; --no-dashboard)

Renaming Fields

prime-rl removes old spellings instead of aliasing them. An old key then fails as an unknown key. If a config from an older version fails to load, look up the new name with --help; do not add aliases or mode="before" translators.

Key Files

  • packages/prime-rl-configs/src/prime_rl/configs/ — all config classes
  • configs/debug/ — minimal debug configs (including configs/debug/eval/*.toml)
  • examples/ — full example configs

documents.label: Evaluating Models with `uv run eval`
documents.html:
Evaluating Models with uv run eval

uv run eval scores a model on one or more verifiers environments and exits after one epoch per source. It reuses the orchestrator's eval pipeline: one env server per source, adaptive or pinned concurrency, every episode written to the trace stream, and --resume support. Config class: EvalConfig (configs/eval.py); uv run eval -h lists every field.

Serving the Model

uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B                              # base model
uv run inference --vllm.model outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_20/weights  # exported checkpoint
curl http://localhost:8000/health
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/models

Without --client.base_url, the eval targets Prime Inference.

Single-Source Shorthands

uv run eval gsm8k -n 32 -r 4
uv run eval gsm8k -n 32 -r 4 -m Qwen/Qwen3-4B --client.base_url http://localhost:8000/v1
uv run eval gsm8k -n 32 -r 4 -c 8 --env.agent.harness.id bash
FlagField
<taskset-id>The single source's env.taskset.id
-n Nselect.limit
-sselect.shuffle
-r Ngroup_size (rollouts per task)
-m MODELmodel
-c NPins concurrency.min_inflight = max_inflight = N
--env.<field> <value>Any field of the env block

Shorthands cannot be combined with a TOML that defines [[source]] blocks. Always cap smoke evals with -n and -r.

Multi-Source TOML

The eval block is flattened to the top level. Per-source select, group_size and sampling override the top-level defaults.

model = "Qwen/Qwen3-4B"
group_size = 4

[select]
limit = 32

[client]
base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1"

[sampling]
max_completion_tokens = 1024

[[source]]
env.taskset.id = "gsm8k"
env.agent.harness.id = "bash"

[[source]]
env.taskset.id = "aime25"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"
uv run eval @ eval.toml --run.name my-eval
uv run eval @ eval.toml --run.name my-eval --resume     # continue an interrupted eval
uv run eval @ eval.toml --dry-run
uv run eval @ eval.toml --monitors.prime                # stream results to the platform

Concurrency: an external API has no vLLM /metrics, so pin it (-c). Against uv run inference, set min_inflight < max_inflight in [concurrency] to adapt to KV-cache usage.

Ready-made configs live in configs/debug/eval/ (single-turn, multi-turn, resume, multi-env, aime2026, tb2).

Selecting Tasks

Steps run in a fixed order: include / exclude (by idx, ids, keys or names), then shuffle (with seed, default 0), then skip, then limit.

uv run eval gsm8k -n 50                                    # first 50 tasks
uv run eval gsm8k -n 50 -s                                 # a fixed random 50
uv run eval gsm8k -n 50 -s --select.seed 1                 # a different random 50
uv run eval gsm8k --select.include.idx 0:10,42             # by position
uv run eval terminal-bench-2 --select.include.names '["fix-git"]'
uv run eval terminal-bench-2 --select.exclude.keys '["<task.key>"]'

Because shuffle runs before limit, resuming a -n 50 -s eval with -n 100 keeps the 50 finished tasks and adds 50 more.

The same select block works for training sources, which gives disjoint train and test splits:

[[orchestrator.eval.source]]
env.taskset.id = "gsm8k"
select.include.idx = [":100"]

[[orchestrator.train.source]]
env.taskset.id = "gsm8k"
select.exclude.idx = [":100"]

Monitoring an Eval

The console stays quiet; everything goes to files and the dashboard.

<run_dir>/
├── configs/latest/            # command.txt, launch TOML, resolved/eval.json
├── logs/latest/eval.log
├── logs/latest/envs/eval/<name>.log
└── monitors/file/             # metrics.jsonl, trace stream, traces/live/
tail -F <run_dir>/logs/latest/eval.log
grep SUCCESS <run_dir>/logs/latest/eval.log      # one "Evaluated <env> ... Reward 0.xxxx" per source
grep -E "WARNING|ERROR" <run_dir>/logs/latest/eval.log <run_dir>/logs/latest/envs/eval/*.log
  • Metrics: eval/<env>/all/<agent>/reward/mean, is_truncated/mean (raise sampling.max_completion_tokens when high), has_error/mean, and taskset metrics.
  • A rollout stuck in boot waits on its sandbox; one in running with a frozen turn count waits on a model call or tool.
  • Read a few traces in the dashboard before trusting a mean reward.
  • Stop with SIGINT/SIGTERM to the PRL::Eval process. On --resume, keep model, sampling and env config the same so finished episodes stay comparable.

documents.label: Installing prime-rl
documents.html:
Installing prime-rl

prime-rl is a uv monorepo with git submodules (verifiers, renderers, prime-envs, pydantic-config). It needs Linux with at least one NVIDIA GPU and Python 3.12 (managed by uv). Upstream tests on RTX 3090/4090/5090, A100, H100, H200 and B200.

Quick Setup

curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

The script clones the repo, initializes submodules recursively, installs uv, and runs uv sync --all-extras.

Manual Setup

git clone https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl.git
cd prime-rl
git submodule update --init -- deps/verifiers deps/renderers deps/prime-envs deps/pydantic-config
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv sync --all-extras

For an existing clone that already tracks every submodule, git submodule update --init --recursive also works (it additionally pulls deps/prime-kernels).

Validate the Install

uv run python -V                                  # Python 3.12.x
uv run python -c "import flash_attn"              # attention kernels present
uv run sft @ configs/debug/fake/sft.toml          # trainer works (1 GPU)
uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B     # inference works (1 GPU)
uv run rl @ examples/basic/reverse-text/rl.toml   # full RL stack (2 GPUs)

Optional logins:

uv run wandb login          # or export WANDB_API_KEY=...
uv run hf auth login        # or export HF_TOKEN=... for gated models and datasets

uv sync Variants

CommandInstalls
uv syncSlim core
uv sync --group devCore + pytest, ruff, pre-commit (run uv run pre-commit install once)
uv sync --all-extrasCore + every extra (gpu, dashboard, dynamo, flash-attn, flash-attn-cute, disagg, quack, sonic-moe, flash-mla, kernels)
uv sync --all-extras --all-packagesAbove + every environment package
uv sync --all-extras --package prime-rl --package gsm8kCore + extras + one environment

Environment Packages

Environments are uv workspace members and are opt-in.

  • Packages under deps/prime-envs/environments/*/* are auto-discovered. Adding one there needs no pyproject.toml edit.
  • verifiers' example envs are listed explicitly in [tool.uv.workspace].members. Add a path there to use another one.
  • A plain uv sync or uv sync --all-extras does not install members, and removes them if they were installed. Re-run with --all-packages, a --package list, or --inexact.
  • Keep --all-extras on training machines so a targeted --package sync does not prune GPU deps.
  • If two envs pin conflicting transitive versions, add one of them to [tool.uv.workspace].exclude.

Check that an env imports before launching a run that uses it:

uv run python -c "import importlib.util; print(importlib.util.find_spec('r2e_gym'))"

The reverse-text env ships inside the verifiers submodule, so the smoke run needs no extra package.

Optional Extras

ExtraCommandProvides
kernelsuv sync --extra kernelsPrebuilt prime-kernels CUDA wheels
gpuuv sync --extra gpuMamba2 SSD kernels for NemotronH (no nvcc needed)
disagguv sync --extra disaggPrebuilt DeepEP wheel for expert parallelism
dashboarduv sync --extra dashboardDashboard without the GPU stack (head nodes)

Verify DeepEP with uv run python -c 'import deep_ep; print(deep_ep.__file__)'.

Source builds are manual and need a CUDA toolkit matching torch:

git submodule update --init deps/prime-kernels
uv pip install --no-build-isolation -e deps/prime-kernels                         # kernels
bash deps/prime-kernels/scripts/install_ep_kernels.sh --wheel-dir /tmp/prime-kernels-wheels
uv pip install --reinstall --no-deps /tmp/prime-kernels-wheels/deep_ep-*.whl      # DeepEP

Set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST when the build host has no GPU or must target several architectures. A source build overrides the wheel until the next uv sync.

llm-d Router

Multi-node or disaggregated deployments can use the llm-d Endpoint Picker instead of vllm-router ([inference.router] type = "llm-d"). Install its binaries once:

bash scripts/install_llmd.sh   # writes third_party/llmd/bin/{epp,envoy,pd-sidecar}

Dependency Rules

  • Add dependencies to pyproject.toml, then run uv sync --all-extras to lock them.
  • Pin git dependencies with a 7-character commit hash in rev.
  • Never edit .venv/; changes are overwritten by the next sync.
  • The workspace uses exclude-newer = "7 days". To bump a package past that window, add it to [tool.uv.exclude-newer-package] before refreshing uv.lock.

documents.label: Monitoring a prime-rl Run
documents.html:
Monitoring a prime-rl Run

Agent Runbook

Use this when a researcher asks an agent to watch a run.

On launch

  1. Find the run dir: <output_dir>/<run_name>. If you only know the output dir, take the newest subdirectory (ls -t outputs | head -1) or read run.name from the launch command.
  2. Read configs/latest/command.txt and configs/latest/resolved/ (start with rl.json, or orchestrator.json on local runs).
  3. Confirm every process is alive and steps are advancing.
  4. Write an initial summary to <run_dir>/STATUS.md.

Recurring check-ins (default every hour)

Confirm processes, grep logs, note the step and key metrics, then append (never overwrite):

## 2026-10-14 09:00 UTC

**Step**: 140 / 500
**Health**: Healthy

**Progress**: reward/mean 0.62 (up from 0.41), truncation 3%, eval avg@4 0.58.
**Stability**: entropy flat, mismatch_kl 0.002, grad_norm no spikes.
**Performance**: trainer 41 s/step, wait_for_batch 2 s; no inference pressure.

**Notes**: 3 sandbox timeouts in envs/train/swe.log, not growing.

Restarts

Never restart unless the researcher explicitly asked, and never run kill or launch commands yourself. Give the researcher the exact command; after they restart, verify all processes are back and progress resumed.

Where Things Live

PathContents
configs/latest/command.txt, launch TOML, resolved/*.json (one attempt_<n> per launch)
logs/latest/Current attempt's logs; resumes never overwrite earlier attempts
monitors/file/metrics.jsonlEvery metric row, tagged by producer
monitors/file/traces/Episode stream, indexes, annotations, live/ in-flight rollouts
launcher/logs/SLURM batch logs (SLURM runs only)

Logs

logs/latest/
├── trainer.log          # rank 0
├── orchestrator.log
├── inference.log        # vLLM (and router on single node)
├── eval.log             # SFT online eval or `uv run eval`
├── trainer/node_*.log, trainer/torchrun/<rdzv>/attempt_0/<rank>/{stdout,stderr}.log
├── inference/node_*.log, inference/router.log   # multi-node only
└── envs/{train,eval}/<env>.log                  # one per env server
tail -F <run_dir>/logs/latest/{trainer,orchestrator,inference}.log
grep -E "WARNING|ERROR" <run_dir>/logs/latest/{trainer,orchestrator,eval,inference}.log
grep -E "WARNING|ERROR" <run_dir>/logs/latest/envs/{train,eval}/*.log
grep -E "WARNING|ERROR" <run_dir>/launcher/logs/*job_*.log      # SLURM

Env logs are the first place to look for rollout errors; most user code runs there. Raise verbosity with orchestrator.log.vf_level = "debug".

Processes

PRL::Launcher
├── PRL::Inference          (vLLM, GPU 0)
├── PRL::EnvServer          (one per train/eval source)
│   └── Verifiers::EnvWorker0..N
├── PRL::Orchestrator       (CPU only)
└── torchrun
    └── PRL::Trainer        (GPU 1+)

ps aux | grep PRL:: lists them. Multi-node runs put trainer and inference on separate nodes.

Metrics

Rollout metrics follow {scope}/{subset}/<agent>/<metric>/<stat>: scope is train/agg, train/<env> or eval/<env>; subset is all or effective (admitted, clean, trainable). Most single-agent envs name their agent agent.

Progress (orchestrator)

MetricMeaning
train/agg/effective/<agent>/reward/meanMain signal; should trend up
train/agg/effective/<agent>/is_truncated/meanTruncated share; raise max_completion_tokens if high
train/agg/all/<agent>/has_error/meanErrored rollouts; sustained > 5% is a smell
train/agg/all/<agent>/is_admitted/meanCurriculum admission rate
train/agg/effective/num_turns/mean, num_total_tokens/meanEpisode size
train/<env>/effective/<agent>/metrics/<name>/meanEnv-specific metrics
eval/<env>/effective/<agent>/{avg@k,pass@k}Online eval scores

Stability (trainer)

MetricMeaning
mismatch_kl/all/{mean,std,max}Trainer vs inference policy KL; a growing mean warns of off-policy collapse
entropy/all/meanToo low means mode collapse; too high means no commitment
is_masked/meanShare of tokens masked by the IPO trust region
optim/grad_normSpikes precede divergence; lower LR or revisit the loss

Performance

SourceMetricReading
trainertime/wait_for_batchHigh: orchestrator/inference is the bottleneck, add inference
orchestratortime/wait_for_policyHigh: trainer is the bottleneck, add trainer GPUs
trainerperf/throughput, perf/mfu, perf/peak_memoryTokens/s, MFU, memory
orchestratoroff_policy/{mean,max}, off_policy/droppedStaleness of trained rollouts

Both processes log a warning when their wait time exceeds active time. Live vLLM stats come from the engine port, not the router:

curl -s http://localhost:8100/metrics | grep -E "num_requests|gpu_cache_usage"

vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc near 1.0 means the KV cache is saturated.

SFT metrics

loss/mean, loss/perplexity (should fall), val/loss, optim/grad_norm, optim/lr, progress/epoch, perf/throughput, and for MoE max_vio/* and expert_load/*.

Dashboard

Launchers auto-start one dashboard daemon per user (PRL::Dashboard) and print a Dashboard · <url> banner. The port can differ from 7788 when taken:

cat ~/.cache/prime-rl/dashboard/daemon.json   # {"pid": ..., "url": "http://localhost:<port>"}
curl -sf <url>/api/runs                       # liveness
uv run dashboard outputs/ other-outputs/      # manual start; read-only on run dirs
uv sync --extra dashboard && uv run dashboard # head node without the GPU stack

Views: overview (W&B-style sections from metrics.jsonl), all metrics, resolved configs, a trace viewer with per-token overlays (advantage, entropy, mismatch, IPO mask), merged logs, and reports. --no-dashboard opts a run out.

W&B and Platform

uv run rl @ rl.toml --monitors.wandb.project my-proj --monitors.wandb.name run-42
uv run rl @ rl.toml --monitors.prime        # Prime Lab; needs PRIME_API_KEY and an enabled team
uv run rl @ rl.toml --no-monitors.file      # disable local metrics/traces (on by default)

Trainer and orchestrator share one W&B run, so monitors.wandb.offline must stay false. Each project gets an auto-created overview saved view with train, eval, stability and performance sections.

Reading Traces

uv run python -m prime_rl.monitors.file.traces <run_dir>              # live rollouts by phase
uv run python -m prime_rl.monitors.file.traces <run_dir> <trace_id>   # one assembled live trace
zstd -dcf <run_dir>/monitors/file/traces/stream/* | jq '.traces[].rewards'
zstd -dcf <run_dir>/monitors/file/traces/stream/* | jq 'select(.ok | not) | {id, env: .env.id, errors}'

Common Failures

ComponentTypical causes
Env workersExceptions in env code, timeouts, sandbox errors, OOM kills (most common)
OrchestratorEmpty or errored rollout spikes, weight-broadcast failures, checkpoint errors
TrainerNCCL/CUDA errors, OOM, NaN loss or gradients
InferenceNCCL/CUDA errors, OOM, request timeouts

A few warnings are normal. Escalate when errors persist, grow, or hit a large share of rollouts.

documents.label: Scaling: GPUs, Nodes, SLURM, Parallelism, LoRA and Inference
documents.html:
Scaling: GPUs, Nodes, SLURM, Parallelism, LoRA and Inference

Single-Node GPU Split

[deployment] defaults to type = "single_node" with 1 trainer GPU and 1 inference GPU. The launcher assigns visible GPUs (from CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) to inference first, then the trainer. Train + inference GPUs must not exceed gpus_per_node (8).

[deployment]
num_train_gpus = 2
num_infer_gpus = 6

[inference.vllm]
tensor_parallel_size = 1

inference.vllm.data_parallel_size is derived automatically as num_infer_gpus // tensor_parallel_size, so you do not need to pass it. NCCL weight broadcast on a single node needs at least 2 GPUs.

Multi-Node with SLURM

[deployment]
type = "multi_node"
num_train_nodes = 2
num_infer_nodes = 2

[slurm]
job_name = "math-qwen30b"
partition = "all"

[inference.vllm]
tensor_parallel_size = 8
uv run rl @ math.toml --dry-run      # writes <run_dir>/launcher/rl.sbatch and resolved configs
uv run rl @ math.toml                # submits with sbatch
  • Multi-node requires [slurm]. Any [slurm] table (or a --slurm.<field> override, or a bare --slurm) switches the launch to sbatch.
  • [slurm] fields: job_name, partition, account, time, nodelist, exclude, project_dir = ".", pre_run_command, template_path, shared_fs = true, launch_modelexpress = true, cleanup_grace_period = 3600.
  • Templates live in src/prime_rl/templates/ (single_node_rl.sbatch.j2, multi_node_rl.sbatch.j2, inference.sbatch.j2); override with --slurm.template-path.
  • Multi-node fields: num_train_nodes (required), num_infer_nodes (inferred from inference.deployment if unset; 0 means trainer-only and needs trainer.data.fake), num_infer_replicas = 1, nodes_per_fsdp_group (sets trainer.model.dp_replicate), orchestrator_on_inference = false.
  • Scripts and batch logs land in <run_dir>/launcher/. Always --dry-run first: validators fail fast there instead of after queueing.

SFT has its own deployment: single_node (num_train_gpus, num_infer_gpus) or multi_node (num_train_nodes = 2, num_infer_nodes = 0, nodes_per_fsdp_group). With online evals, the first num_infer_nodes nodes run inference and the rest run the trainer.

Trainer Parallelism

Set under [trainer.model] in RL and [model] in SFT.

FieldDefaultNotes
dp_replicate1HSDP replicate dimension
reshard_after_forwardtrueFSDP resharding
offload"optimizer""none", "optimizer", "full" (full: adamw or sign_sgd only, disables grad clipping)
ep"auto"Expert parallel: min(world_size // dp_replicate, 8) for MoE, else 1
cp1Context parallel; needs flash attention
cp_style"ring""ring" or "ulysses" (VLMs require ulysses)
attn"auto"flash_attention_2, flash_attention_3, flash_attention_4
acfull, freq 1Activation checkpointing (mode = "full" or "selective")
ac_offloadingmax_inflight_activations = 5Offload checkpointed activations
compileon[trainer.model.compile] fullgraph, mode
moe.compute.type"bf16""deepgemm_fp8", "mxfp8"
moe.dispatch.type"torch""deepep" needs the disagg extra
freeze_moe_routerauto (true in RL)Keeps inference and trainer expert choices aligned
optimization_dtype, reduce_dtype"float32"Do not change unless explicitly asked
[trainer.model]
attn = "flash_attention_3"
ep = 8
cp = 2
cp_style = "ulysses"

[trainer.model.compile]

[trainer.model.ac_offloading]

Throughput recipes in docs/scaling.md are written with SFT paths ([model], [model.compile]); in RL put the same keys under [trainer.model].

LoRA

[trainer.model.lora]     # [model.lora] in SFT
rank = 32
alpha = 64
dropout = 0.0
  • Defaults: rank = 16, alpha = 32.0, target_modules covering q/k/v/o, MLP and expert projections across families (unknown names are ignored).
  • rl sets inference.vllm.enable_lora = true and max_lora_rank (rounded up to 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 320 or 512) for you. An external server must be started with those flags.
  • LoRA uses filesystem weight broadcast. Leaving [weight_broadcast] unset selects it automatically; setting type = "nccl" or "nixl" together with LoRA raises an error.
  • modules_to_save is rejected for real training (the broadcast ships only adapters).
  • Export via convert_dcp_to_bf16.py rejects LoRA checkpoints.

Examples: examples/basic/alphabet-sort/rl.toml (r32, α64) and examples/basic/wiki-search/rl.toml (r8).

Weight Broadcast and Rollout Transport

[weight_broadcast] typeFieldsWhen
nccl (rl default)host, port = 29501, timeoutDefault when [inference] is set and no LoRA
filesystemtimeout = 3600LoRA, or no managed inference
nixlport = 8001, host, session_idNeeds NIXL + ModelExpress installs

[rollout_transport] type = "zmq" (default, port 5555) ships batches in memory; "filesystem" writes <run_dir>/batches/step_<n>/rank_<r>.bin.

Inference Server

uv run inference wraps vLLM with a router. Standalone configs put server, vllm, router, deployment, slurm at the top level; inside rl they live under [inference.*].

uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --vllm.enforce-eager
uv run inference --vllm.model Qwen/Qwen3-32B --server.port 8001 --vllm.tensor-parallel-size 2
SettingDefaultNotes
server.port8000Client-facing router URL
backend_portserver.port + 100Engine; admin calls and /metrics go here
vllm.gpu_memory_utilization0.9
vllm.tool_call_parser, vllm.reasoning_parser"auto"Resolved from the model name
router.type"vllm-router"Policy sticky_least_loaded; "llm-d" only for multi-node/disaggregated
kv_cache_offload.typenone"native" or "mooncake" (needs cpu.num_bytes)

Any other vLLM argument goes under [inference.vllm] as-is (max_num_seqs, max_model_len, ...).

Custom endpoints on the engine: POST /update_weights, /load_lora_adapter, /init_broadcaster, /pause, /resume, and GET /liveness.

Inference deployments

[inference.deployment] typeFields
single_node (default)none
multi_nodenum_nodes = 2; needs [slurm]
disaggregatedprefill_nodes_per_replica, decode_nodes_per_replica, num_prefill_replicas, num_decode_replicas, prefill_port = 8100, decode_port = 8200; needs [slurm]

Disaggregated prefill/decode turns on expert parallel and NIXL KV transfer automatically. Install NIXL with bash scripts/install_nixl_from_source.sh and ModelExpress with bash scripts/install_modelexpress.sh, and re-run them after every uv sync.

External inference

Omit [inference] in the RL config and set [orchestrator.model.client] base_url. The server must be uv run inference (or a Dynamo deployment, see examples/extra/dynamo/rl.toml). Start it with LoRA flags or --vllm.enable-return-routed-experts when the run needs them; prime-rl only warns.

Other Features

  • VLM: [model.vlm] (freeze_vision_encoder = true); only Qwen3.5 dense and MoE are registered, bf16 dtypes required, unfrozen vision encoder cannot combine with LoRA.
  • Router replay (MoE): trainer.enable_router_replay = true turns on routed-expert return in vLLM. Not supported with disaggregated P/D, llm-d or KV offload.
  • Adaptive concurrency: [orchestrator.concurrency] with min_inflight = 1, max_inflight = 1024, optional initial_inflight.

Reference Multi-Node Configs

PathLayout
examples/advanced/qwen3-30b-a3b/math.tomlQwen3-30B-A3B RL, 2 train + 2 inference nodes, ep 8
examples/advanced/qwen3-30b-a3b/swe.tomlr2e-gym with bash harness, 131k context, ep 8, cp 2
examples/advanced/glm-4.5-air/swe-budget.toml1 + 1 nodes with sign_sgd; overlays for 2 and 4 nodes
examples/advanced/glm-5.3/swe.toml16 train nodes, disaggregated prefill/decode
examples/advanced/intellect-3.1/rl.toml4 train + 12 inference nodes, muon, multi-env
configs/advanced/nemotron-3-super/swe.tomlNemotron-3-Super-120B RL

documents.label: Launching, Checkpointing, Resuming and Exporting Runs
documents.html:
Launching, Checkpointing, Resuming and Exporting Runs

Entrypoints

CommandConfig classPurpose
uv run rlRLConfig (configs/rl.py)Inference + orchestrator + trainer in one launch
uv run sftSFTConfig (configs/sft.py)Dataset SFT; runs torchrun internally
uv run inferenceInferenceConfig (configs/inference.py)vLLM server with weight-update endpoints
uv run evalEvalConfig (configs/eval.py)Standalone evals (see eval.md)
uv run orchestratorOrchestratorConfigStandalone orchestrator for manual layouts
uv run trainerTrainerConfigStandalone RL trainer
uv run env-serverEnvServerConfigOne env server; rl starts these automatically

All accept @ file.toml plus CLI overrides and --dry-run. Never call torchrun for SFT or vllm serve for inference.

RL

uv run rl @ examples/basic/reverse-text/rl.toml
uv run rl @ my-rl.toml --run.name exp-1 --max-steps 200 --ckpt.interval 50 \
  --monitors.wandb.project my-proj --monitors.wandb.name exp-1
uv run rl @ my-rl.toml --dry-run --run.name check   # resolve, validate, write configs, exit

Most-tuned knobs

KnobDefaultNotes
max_stepsNoneTrainer steps
seq_lenNoneShared sequence length
orchestrator.batch_size128Rollouts per trainer step; 64 minimum, 1024+ in production
orchestrator.train.group_size1Rollouts per task; set ≥ 8 for group-relative algorithms
orchestrator.train.sampling.temperature1.0Train sampling temperature
orchestrator.train.sampling.max_completion_tokensNoneTruncation cap; watch is_truncated
orchestrator.max_off_policy_steps8Max rollout staleness
orchestrator.eval.interval100Online eval cadence
trainer.optim.lr1e-6type: adamw, muon, sign_sgd; max_norm 1.0
trainer.scheduler.typeconstantlinear / cosine take warmup_steps, min_lr
trainer.lossIPOSee algorithms.md
trainer.model.freeze_moe_routerauto (true in RL)Training the router widens train/inference mismatch
log.level / orchestrator.log.vf_levelinfovf_level = "debug" for env debugging

Using an external inference server

Omit [inference]. rl then starts no server, and the orchestrator talks to orchestrator.model.client.base_url (default http://localhost:8000/v1). Start that server with uv run inference so the weight-update endpoints exist. With LoRA it must also run with --vllm.enable-lora and a matching --vllm.max-lora-rank.

SFT

uv run sft @ examples/basic/reverse-text/sft.toml --monitors.wandb
uv run sft @ sft.toml --slurm.job-name my-sft     # any [slurm] key submits to SLURM
uv run sft @ sft.toml --dry-run

SFT configs are flat: [model], [data], [optim], [scheduler], [val], [eval], [renderer], [deployment] at the top level (RL nests the trainer under [trainer.*]).

KnobWhat it controls
data.nameHF dataset name or local path
data.seq_lenPer-sample sequence length
data.batch_sizeGlobal batch size (default 128); must divide by data.micro_batch_size
data.loss_mask.*Which roles contribute to loss (system, user, assistant, tool)
val.intervalValidation cadence; val.data mirrors data
eval.intervalOnline rollout evals (needs [inference])

Dataset format

  • Prompt-completion: prompt and completion columns; loss only on the completion.
  • Messages: one messages column; loss on assistant turns. Wins if both layouts exist.
  • tools column (OpenAI function format, list or JSON string) for tool-use SFT.
  • message_loss_mask column: one 0/1 per message to select which turns train.
  • Rename columns with [data.columns]:
[data.columns]
messages = "conversation"
tools = "schemas"

Tokenization is renderer-only ([renderer] name = "auto" by default):

[renderer]
name = "qwen3"
enable_thinking = false

Online evals during SFT

[eval]
interval = 25

[eval.select]
limit = 32

[[eval.source]]
name = "reverse-text"
env.taskset.id = "reverse-text"
env.agent.harness.id = "null"
env.agent.runtime.type = "subprocess"

[inference]

[deployment]
num_train_gpus = 1
num_infer_gpus = 1

The base model is evaluated before step 1 (eval.skip_first_step disables it). Weights reach the eval server over NCCL by default; [weight_broadcast] type = "filesystem" reloads from disk.

Run Directories

<output_dir>/<run_name>: output_dir defaults to $PRL_OUTPUT_DIR, else outputs. Without --run.name, the name is <envs>--<model>--<short-id> (SFT: <dataset>--<model>--<short-id>). --run.dir overrides only the directory leaf.

<run_dir>/
├── configs/attempt_<n>/      # command.txt, launch TOML, resolved/*.json  (configs/latest -> current)
├── logs/attempt_<n>/         # trainer.log, orchestrator.log, inference.log, eval.log, envs/  (logs/latest)
├── checkpoints/step_<n>/     # trainer/ (DCP) and orchestrator/
├── monitors/file/            # metrics.jsonl and traces/
├── broadcasts/               # weight-broadcast handshakes
└── launcher/                 # SLURM scripts and batch logs (SLURM only)

Launching into a run dir that already has artifacts fails unless you pass --resume or --clean (which deletes only that run dir).

Checkpointing

Off by default. The trainer saves FSDP-sharded DCP state, optimizer, scheduler and progress; the orchestrator saves progress and per-env data state; inference is stateless.

uv run rl @ rl.toml --ckpt                                        # end of training only
uv run rl @ rl.toml --ckpt.interval 25                            # every 25 steps
uv run rl @ rl.toml --ckpt.interval 25 --ckpt.keep-last 3         # rolling window of 3
uv run rl @ rl.toml --ckpt.interval 25 --ckpt.keep-interval 100   # plus a permanent one every 100
[ckpt]
interval = 25
keep_last = 3
keep_interval = 100

Resuming

Re-run the same command with the same --run.name and --resume:

uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 10 --ckpt --run.name my-run
uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 20 --ckpt --resume --run.name my-run           # latest checkpoint
uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 20 --ckpt --resume.step 10 --run.name my-run   # a specific step
uv run rl @ rl.toml --max-steps 20 --ckpt --run.name my-fork \
  --resume.dir outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_10                               # fork into a new run
  • --max-steps is the absolute final step, not the remaining delta.
  • resume.step and resume.dir are mutually exclusive.
  • Without [ckpt] a resumed run loads the checkpoint but saves no new ones.
  • Trainer checkpoint loading can skip parts: trainer.ckpt.skip_optimizer, skip_scheduler, skip_dataloader.

Exporting Checkpoints

uv run python tools/convert_dcp_to_bf16.py outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_20
uv run torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 tools/convert_dcp_to_bf16.py outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_20
uv run inference --vllm.model outputs/my-run/checkpoints/step_20/weights
  • Output goes to <ckpt_dir>/weights (or a second positional argument), as HF safetensors plus config and tokenizer. The model config is read from the run's resolved config.
  • Full fine-tunes only; LoRA checkpoints are rejected.
  • FP8: tools/convert_bf16_to_fp8.py <dir> or tools/convert_dcp_to_fp8.py <ckpt_dir> (writes <ckpt_dir>/weights-FP8). Dequantize FP8-only releases with tools/convert_fp8_to_bf16.py <dir>.
  • On SM120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000), serve blockwise-FP8 checkpoints with VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel,MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel to avoid a kernel that silently degrades outputs.

Example Configs

PathWhat it shows
examples/basic/reverse-text/{rl,sft,eval}.tomlSingle-turn SFT → RL on Qwen3-0.6B (2 GPUs)
examples/basic/wordle/{rl,sft,eval}.tomlMulti-turn SFT and RL on Qwen3-1.7B
examples/basic/alphabet-sort/rl.tomlMulti-turn RL with LoRA (r32, α64)
examples/basic/wiki-search/rl.tomlTool calling with LoRA, 2 train + 6 inference GPUs
examples/basic/hendrycks-sanity/rl.tomlMath RL sanity check, 4 + 4 GPUs
examples/extra/dynamo/rl.tomlExternal inference server (no [inference])
examples/extra/vlm/sft.tomlVLM SFT with LoRA
examples/advanced/qwen3-30b-a3b/*.tomlMulti-node MoE RL and SFT on SLURM
examples/advanced/glm-4.5-air/ipo-ablation/IPO vs IcePop ablation
configs/debug/algo/*.tomlOne small config per algorithm (grpo, max_rl, opd, sft_distill, echo, rae, ...)
configs/debug/eval/*.tomlEval shapes: single-turn, multi-turn, resume, multi-env

documents.label: SKILL.md
documents.html:
name: scalingo description: > Scalingo is a European (French) Platform-as-a-Service for deploying and operating web applications, background workers, and managed databases. Use this skill whenever the user mentions Scalingo, wants to deploy an app to Scalingo, work with the scalingo CLI, provision addons (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, OpenSearch, InfluxDB), configure review apps, manage the scalingo.json manifest or a Procfile, scale containers, set up log drains, migrate from Heroku, use the Scalingo Terraform provider, or target sovereign regions (osc-fr1, osc-secnum-fr1 on SecNumCloud infrastructure). Also trigger for "deploy a French PaaS", "HDS-compliant hosting", "SecNumCloud deployment", or questions about Scalingo's Heroku-compatible buildpack model.

Scalingo

Scalingo is a European PaaS in the Heroku lineage. You push code (usually via git), the platform builds it with a buildpack, and containers are started according to your Procfile. Managed databases are available as addons. The platform's differentiators are European/French jurisdiction, ISO 27001 / HDS certification, and a region (osc-secnum-fr1) running on SecNumCloud-qualified Outscale infrastructure.

This skill covers the platform end-to-end at a working level: CLI, deployment, addons, scaling, review apps, and IaC. For deep dives on any single topic, consult the references/ files — pointers are given throughout.

When to reach for each reference

The main file stays practical. Pull in a reference when:

  • references/cli-reference.md — user needs a specific CLI command you don't remember, or wants a full command map
  • references/deployment.md — deploying via non-git methods (GitHub/GitLab integration, tarball archive, WAR), or configuring auto-deploy
  • references/addons-databases.md — provisioning, connecting to, or operating a managed database
  • references/scaling-autoscaler.md — configuring horizontal/vertical scaling or the autoscaler's metric targets
  • references/manifest-review-apps.md — writing a scalingo.json, configuring review apps, or building a one-click deploy button
  • references/terraform-iac.md — managing Scalingo resources via the official Terraform provider
  • references/buildpacks.md — understanding stacks, picking or chaining buildpacks, writing a custom buildpack
  • references/tutorials.md — deploying a well-known tool (Keycloak, PostgREST, WordPress, n8n, Metabase, ModSecurity WAF, Judoscale, Lovable, Whisper, pgvector, OpenSearch RAG, Elastic Stack) following the official Tutorials Hub

Mental model

Three nouns to internalize:

  • App — the unit of deployment. Has a name, a region, environment variables, and a git remote. One app = one deployable project. Apps can be grouped into Projects, which also scope Private Networks.
  • Process type — a named command from the Procfile (web, tcp, postdeploy, or anything custom like worker). Each process type runs in one or more containers.
  • Addon — a managed service attached to an app (database, cache). Exposes connection details via env vars like SCALINGO_POSTGRESQL_URL.

Everything else — containers, logs, metrics, domains, collaborators — hangs off an app.

Installation and auth

# Install (macOS/Linux)
curl -O https://cli-dl.scalingo.com/install && bash install

# Log in (opens a browser)
scalingo login

# Or use an API token (for CI/non-interactive)
export SCALINGO_API_TOKEN="tk-us-..."

Set a default region once so you don't repeat --region on every command:

scalingo config --region osc-fr1          # Paris, standard
# OR
scalingo config --region osc-secnum-fr1   # Paris, SecNumCloud infrastructure (sovereign)

Region notes:

  • osc-fr1 — default; hosted on Outscale in Paris
  • osc-secnum-fr1 — runs on Outscale's SecNumCloud-qualified IaaS; used for French public-sector and sensitive workloads. Access is granted through Scalingo support. The Scalingo PaaS layer itself is not (yet) SecNumCloud-qualified; its qualification is in progress
  • List current regions at any time with scalingo regions

Quick start: create and deploy an app

# 1. Create the app (empty, in the default region)
scalingo create my-app

# 2. Add the git remote the CLI printed — or ask for it explicitly:
scalingo --app my-app git-show
git remote add scalingo git@ssh.osc-fr1.scalingo.com:my-app.git

# 3. Push. master OR main are accepted; other branches need mapping:
git push scalingo main
# git push scalingo feature-x:main   # deploy a different local branch

# 4. Watch the build
scalingo --app my-app logs -f

The build detects your stack from files in the repo (Gemfile → Ruby, package.json → Node, requirements.txt/pyproject.toml → Python, etc.) and runs the matching buildpack. Force a buildpack with BUILDPACK_URL if detection is wrong — see references/buildpacks.md.

By default, the web process type scales to 1 × M container. All other process types default to 0 and must be scaled explicitly to start.

The Procfile

A Procfile at repo root declares how each process type starts:

web: gunicorn app:app --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT
worker: celery -A tasks worker --loglevel=INFO
postdeploy: python manage.py migrate

Reserved process types:

  • web — receives HTTP traffic, must bind to $PORT, scaled to 1 by default
  • tcp — receives raw TCP traffic through the TCP gateway addon
  • postdeploy — runs once per deployment in a separate one-off container (size M, 20-minute limit) after the build and before traffic switches to the new containers; use it for migrations. It replaces the deprecated scripts.postdeploy in scalingo.json

There is no release process type on Scalingo (that's Heroku). Migrations belong in postdeploy.

Everything else is a custom process type — scale it to ≥1 to start it:

scalingo --app my-app scale worker:1:M

Common operations (CLI cheatsheet)

The CLI almost always wants --app <name> (or -a <name>). All commands below assume that flag.

# Apps
scalingo apps                        # list your apps
scalingo create my-app               # create (--project-id to place it in a project)
scalingo --app my-app apps-info      # details (stack, region, status)
scalingo rename --app old --new-name new
scalingo destroy --app my-app        # delete (confirmation required)

# Deploy / restart
git push scalingo main               # standard deploy
scalingo --app my-app deploy my-app.tar.gz  # deploy from an archive (local path or URL)
scalingo --app my-app restart                # restart all containers
scalingo --app my-app restart web            # restart one process type

# Environment
scalingo --app my-app env                    # list
scalingo --app my-app env-set KEY=value OTHER=value
scalingo --app my-app env-unset KEY
# NOTE: env changes do NOT auto-restart; add `scalingo restart` after bulk changes.

# Scaling (amount:size syntax)
scalingo --app my-app scale web:2:L worker:1:M
scalingo --app my-app ps                     # current formation

# Logs
scalingo --app my-app logs                   # last lines
scalingo --app my-app logs -f                # stream
scalingo --app my-app logs --lines 500       # historical

# One-off containers (copy of production env, destroyed on exit)
scalingo --app my-app run bash               # interactive shell
scalingo --app my-app run --size XL rake db:migrate
scalingo --app my-app run --detached long-job.sh
scalingo --app my-app cron-tasks             # scheduled jobs declared in cron.json (Scalingo Scheduler)

# Domains + TLS (Let's Encrypt is automatic; certificates last 45 days and renew automatically)
scalingo --app my-app domains-add example.com
scalingo --app my-app domains                # list
scalingo --app my-app set-canonical-domain example.com

# Addons
scalingo --app my-app addons                 # list attached
scalingo --app my-app addons-add postgresql postgresql-starter-512
scalingo --app my-app addons-upgrade <addon-id> postgresql-business-1024

# Machine-readable output (global flag; not every command supports it yet)
scalingo --format json --app my-app apps-info

For the full command surface, see references/cli-reference.md.

Environment variables

All configuration belongs in env (12-factor). Scalingo injects addon connection strings automatically — e.g. attaching PostgreSQL gives you SCALINGO_POSTGRESQL_URL and aliases it to DATABASE_URL. Your app reads these at runtime.

scalingo --app my-app env-set DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=myapp.settings.prod

Changing env variables does not trigger a restart. Batch your changes, then scalingo restart.

For multi-line values (TLS keys, JSON blobs), either quote carefully or Base64-encode and decode in-app — the dashboard won't render multi-line values cleanly. Limits: names up to 64 characters, values up to 32,768 characters.

Addons in one minute

# Discover what's available and see plans
scalingo addons-list
scalingo addons-plans postgresql

# Attach
scalingo --app my-app addons-add postgresql postgresql-starter-512

# Connect from a one-off (uses injected env vars)
scalingo --app my-app pgsql-console
scalingo --app my-app mongo-console
scalingo --app my-app redis-console

Main engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis (marketed as "Scalingo for Caching"; the addon ID is still redis), OpenSearch, InfluxDB. Elasticsearch is being phased out in favour of OpenSearch, and Sandbox plans can no longer be created. Plans come in service classes: Starter (single node, 98% SLA), Business (multi-node HA, 99.96%), and Enterprise (99.99%, PostgreSQL on Dedicated Resources only, in preview). Always confirm plan IDs with scalingo addons-plans <addon> before using them. Details and sizing guidance: references/addons-databases.md.

scalingo.json (app manifest)

An optional file at repo root that declares how an app should be built when created from a one-click deploy button or as a review app. Minimal shape:

{
  "name": "My App",
  "env": {
    "SECRET_KEY": { "generator": "secret" },
    "PUBLIC_URL": { "generator": "url" }
  },
  "formation": {
    "web":    { "amount": 1, "size": "M" },
    "worker": { "amount": 1, "size": "M" }
  },
  "addons": [
    { "plan": "postgresql:postgresql-starter-512" },
    { "plan": "redis:redis-starter-256" }
  ],
  "scripts": {
    "first-deploy": "bundle exec rake db:migrate db:seed"
  }
}

Triggers for this file: review apps, one-click deploy buttons. It is read only when such an app is created, and not applied on ordinary git push deploys — set the production formation/addons explicitly once. See references/manifest-review-apps.md.

Scaling and the autoscaler

Two dimensions:

  • Horizontal — scalingo scale web:3:M (three M-sized web containers). Load is balanced across them.
  • Vertical — scalingo scale web:1:XL (upgrade the container tier). Sizes: S / M / L / XL / 2XL / 3XL; 3XL (8 GiB) is the largest and is self-service. Memory doubles per tier: 256 MiB → 512 MiB → 1 GiB → 2 GiB → 4 GiB → 8 GiB. By default a process type can run up to 10 containers.

Swap is being removed: new apps no longer get it since 2026-09-01, and all containers lose it on 2027-01-01. Size containers so the app fits in RAM.

The Scalingo Autoscaler adjusts horizontal scale automatically based on a target metric (cpu, memory, swap, rpm_per_container, p95_response_time, 5XX). It needs a minimum of 2 containers, is keyed by container type (autoscalers-add -c web -m cpu -t 0.75 --min-containers 2 --max-containers 10), and cooldowns prevent flapping (1 min out, 3 min in). Full config and metric guidance: references/scaling-autoscaler.md.

Logs and observability

  • Live tail: scalingo --app my-app logs -f
  • Router logs (HTTP-level) are off by default — enable in dashboard Routing settings
  • Files rotate at 50 MiB to Log Archives (fetch via dashboard or CLI, paginated)
  • Ingest caps: 64 MiB/min/container and 16,384 lines/min/container — excess lines are dropped for the rest of the minute
  • Archived logs are kept for 1 year
  • For retention beyond archives or for search/alerting, configure a Log Drain (syslog/HTTPS/ELK endpoint)

Deployment options beyond git

When git-push isn't the right fit:

  • GitHub / GitLab integration — link a repo, auto-deploy a branch, enable review apps per PR/MR
  • Archive deploy — scalingo --app my-app deploy my-app.tar.gz (the archive must contain the code inside a single top-level folder, whatever its name). There is no deploy-from-Docker-image option
  • WAR — scalingo --app my-app deploy --war app.war for a prebuilt Java WAR
  • One-click deploy button — a URL that deploys a scalingo.json-equipped repo

Details and exact URL formats: references/deployment.md.

Infrastructure as code (Terraform)

The official Scalingo Terraform provider (Scalingo/scalingo) covers apps (including their env vars), addons, container types, autoscalers, domains, SCM integrations, collaborators, log drains, alerts, projects, firewall rules, and Dedicated Resources databases. Useful when you need reproducible environments or multiple review/staging stacks.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    scalingo = { source = "Scalingo/scalingo", version = "~> 2.0" }
  }
}

provider "scalingo" {
  region = "osc-fr1"   # or env: SCALINGO_REGION
  # api_token via env: SCALINGO_API_TOKEN
}

data "scalingo_stack" "s26" {
  name = "scalingo-26"
}

resource "scalingo_app" "api" {
  name     = "my-api"
  stack_id = data.scalingo_stack.s26.id   # Scalingo's own tutorials also pass the slug directly
  environment = {
    NODE_ENV = "production"
  }
}

resource "scalingo_addon" "db" {
  provider_id = "postgresql"
  plan        = "postgresql-starter-512"
  app         = scalingo_app.api.id
}

Full resource catalog and the opinionated community module (scalingo-community/app/scalingo): references/terraform-iac.md.

Choosing a region

Use caseRegionNotes
Default / general web appsosc-fr1Paris, Outscale infrastructure, ISO 27001
French public sector, sensitive data, ANSSI complianceosc-secnum-fr1SecNumCloud-qualified Outscale infrastructure, stricter access controls, access via support
Health data (HDS)osc-fr1 + HDS-eligible plansCertification covers hosting, not your app logic

Set once: scalingo config --region osc-secnum-fr1. Each CLI call also accepts --region to override.

Migrating from Heroku

Scalingo is intentionally compatible with the Heroku workflow: Procfile, buildpacks (mostly unchanged), heroku run → scalingo run, app.json → scalingo.json (same shape for the fields that matter). Heroku's release: Procfile line becomes postdeploy:. Typical migration steps:

  1. Create the app on Scalingo and add its git remote alongside Heroku's
  2. Provision matching addons (and copy data — pg_dump/pg_restore for PostgreSQL, etc.)
  3. Copy env vars (heroku config -s → scalingo env-set)
  4. Push; verify; cut over DNS

A common gotcha: Scalingo's git deploy accepts only master and main — map other branches with local-branch:main syntax.

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

  • New process type doesn't start after deploy — every process type except web defaults to 0. Run scalingo scale <name>:1:M.
  • env-set seemed to have no effect — env changes don't auto-restart. Run scalingo restart.
  • Push rejected — Scalingo git only accepts master or main. Use git push scalingo mybranch:main.
  • Attached one-off container disconnects — it is closed after 30 minutes with no data exchanged, and any one-off is killed after 1 hour with no output. Use --detached and log progress for long jobs. If it never connects, check that your network allows the outbound connection the CLI opens.
  • Migrations put in a release: line never run — Scalingo has no release type; use postdeploy:.
  • Build works locally but fails on Scalingo — the default stack is scalingo-26 (Ubuntu 26.04); scalingo-24 is also supported and scalingo-22 is deprecated (shut down 2027-06-01). Native dependencies compiled on your Mac won't transfer; the buildpack rebuilds them from source. Pin versions in lockfiles.
  • Logs suddenly quiet — you may have hit the 64 MiB/min/container ingest cap. Reduce verbosity or add containers.
  • Review app has production credentials — by default review apps inherit parent env. Override in scalingo.json (see references/manifest-review-apps.md).

Compliance quick facts

Scalingo holds ISO 27001:2022 (information security) and HDS 2.0 (French health data hosting). The osc-secnum-fr1 region runs on Outscale infrastructure that is SecNumCloud-qualified (ANSSI's qualification for trusted cloud providers). Scalingo's own PaaS layer is not SecNumCloud-qualified yet; its qualification is in progress, so don't describe a Scalingo deployment as "SecNumCloud-qualified" end to end. Hosting is in France, under European jurisdiction.

Certification applies to the platform; your application's data handling is still your responsibility.

When working on a Scalingo task, check the relevant reference before answering from memory — addon plan names, Terraform resource schemas, and autoscaler metric names change over time, and the references carry the current specifics.

When to Use / Not Use

Use this skill when:

  • Deploying or operating an app on Scalingo (git push, GitHub/GitLab integration, archives)
  • Provisioning managed addons (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, OpenSearch, InfluxDB)
  • Scaling containers, configuring the autoscaler, or setting up review apps / scalingo.json
  • Managing infrastructure with the Scalingo Terraform provider
  • Migrating from Heroku or targeting French compliance (HDS, osc-secnum-fr1 on SecNumCloud infrastructure)

Do NOT use this skill when:

  • Deploying to a different platform — Vercel, Railway, or plain Kubernetes are out of scope
  • The task is purely local development with no deployment component
  • The user wants a generic Docker orchestration answer that isn't Scalingo-specific — prefer the platform they're actually on

documents.label: Addons and Managed Databases
documents.html:
Addons and Managed Databases

Scalingo addons are managed services attached to an app. Each attachment injects connection credentials as env vars. The main category is managed databases; others include caching services, email relays, and APM integrations.

Table of contents

  1. How addons work
  2. PostgreSQL
  3. MySQL
  4. MongoDB
  5. Scalingo for Caching (Redis)
  6. OpenSearch
  7. InfluxDB and Elasticsearch (phasing out)
  8. Backups
  9. Service classes and sizing
  10. Shared infrastructure vs dedicated
  11. Architecture and networking
  12. Migration and import

How addons work

Sandbox plans can no longer be created (since 2026-03-02); the smallest plan of each engine is now a Starter plan. Always confirm plan IDs with scalingo addons-plans <provider> before writing them into scripts, manifests, or Terraform.

Attaching an addon:

scalingo --app my-app addons-add <provider> <plan>
# e.g.
scalingo --app my-app addons-add postgresql postgresql-starter-512

On success:

  • An addon ID (ad-<uuid>) is assigned
  • Connection env vars are injected into the app (e.g. SCALINGO_POSTGRESQL_URL)
  • For single-DB setups, DATABASE_URL is aliased to the primary DB URL
  • The app is not restarted automatically — do so manually after attaching

Listing and inspecting:

scalingo --app my-app addons                      # list
scalingo --app my-app addons-info <addon-id>      # details + status
scalingo --app my-app addons-plans <provider>     # available plans

Upgrading/downgrading plans happens with minimal downtime on single-node plans and zero downtime on HA plans:

scalingo --app my-app addons-upgrade <addon-id> postgresql-business-1024
